recipeInstructions.text: Spoon the finished dip back into the empty Grillo's tub. This is the visual hook — the dip lives in the original pickle tub. Smooth the top with the back of a spoon.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Straight from the Grillo's tub. Pair with Wilde Protein Chips for the high-protein combo (270 cal / 27g protein per serving), or use regular tortilla chips, carrots, celery, cucumber slices, or any crunchy dipper. Refrigerate leftovers in the tub with the lid back on; eat within 3-4 days.

recipe.name: Grillo's Pickle Dip + Wilde Chips Combo
recipe.description: 270 cal / 27g protein snack — the dip (110/16) + a bag of Wilde Spicy Queso Protein Chips (160/11). Macro-coded combo of the viral pickle dip remix.
recipeIngredient: 1 generous scoop of High-Protein Grillo's Pickle Dip (~50g, 1/10 of the batch)
1 bag (1.34 oz / ~30 chips) Wilde Spicy Queso Protein Chips

recipeInstructions.name: Make The Dip (one-time, Ahead)
recipeInstructions.text: Follow the [parent dip recipe](/cookbook/grillos-pickle-dip-protein-style) to make a 10-serving batch. Store in the Grillo's tub in the fridge. Each scoop = 110 cal / 16g protein. Skip this step if the dip is already in your fridge.

recipeInstructions.name: Assemble The Combo
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the Grillo's tub from the fridge. Open 1 bag of Wilde Spicy Queso Protein Chips. Dunk chips, eat. One scoop of dip from the tub = the right portion for the macro log.

recipeInstructions.name: Store
recipeInstructions.text: Lid back on the dip tub, sealed clip on the chip bag. The dip holds 3-4 days; chips hold ~3 weeks sealed. Repeat the combo as often as you want — each repeat is 270 / 27.

recipe.name: Ham & Cheese Power Melt
recipe.description: Crispy outside. Layered inside. High-protein comfort.
recipeIngredient: 3 slices 365 Organic Black Forest Uncured Ham (~60 cal)
1 oz Kraft Fat Free Cheddar cheese

recipeInstructions.name: Filmed Option
recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and thoroughly drain the 1 oz fat-free cheddar before layering. The original recipe also works without this step; it does not change the ingredient amount or published macros.

recipeInstructions.name: Layer
recipeInstructions.text: Bread → cheese → ham → cheese → ham → cheese → ham → cheese → bread. The alternating layers are key — even melt throughout.

recipeInstructions.name: Heat
recipeInstructions.text: Nonstick pan on LOW heat. Add butter, let it melt.

recipeInstructions.name: Cook
recipeInstructions.text: Place sandwich in pan. Cook slowly, 3-4 min per side until golden brown. Low heat prevents burning before cheese melts.

recipeInstructions.name: Melt
recipeInstructions.text: Optional — cover with lid for 30-60 seconds to fully melt the cheese.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest
recipeInstructions.text: 1 minute. Slice and serve with mustard.

recipe.name: Ham, Egg & Cheese Protein Bagel
recipe.description: A toasted whole breakfast sandwich with two eggs, warm ham, and two melty cheeses — about 415 calories and 46g protein.
recipeIngredient: 3 slices 365 Black Forest ham (one full serving)

recipeInstructions.name: Toast
recipeInstructions.text: Split and toast the bagel.

recipeInstructions.name: Cook Eggs
recipeInstructions.text: Cook the two eggs in a nonstick pan. No added oil or butter was used in this build.

recipeInstructions.name: Melt + Warm
recipeInstructions.text: Add one Velveeta slice to the eggs and let it melt. Warm the three ham slices with the second cheese slice.

recipeInstructions.name: Stack + Slice
recipeInstructions.text: Spread the Laughing Cow Light wedge on the toasted bagel. Stack eggs, ham and melted cheese, close the sandwich, then slice it.

recipe.name: 2 Protein Dessert Backups When the Creami Isn't Ready
recipe.description: Ninja Creami is my favorite — but it takes planning. When the pint isn't frozen, these are the 2 protein desserts I grab. Choose ONE (do not add together).
recipeIngredient: 1.5 labeled servings Protein Pints Coffee (any Protein Pints flavor works — Coffee is my favorite)
1 Prime Bites Protein Brownie, any flavor (~220 cal / 19g protein per brownie)
1/4 pint lighter or high-protein ice cream — Halo Top, Frozen One, or Protein Pints all work

recipeInstructions.text: OPTION 1 — PROTEIN PINTS COFFEE (180 CAL / 15G PROTEIN): Measure 1.5 labeled servings from a Protein Pints pint (Coffee is my favorite — the best protein ice cream I've tried). Any flavor works. Serve immediately. This is the pick when you want ice cream on its own with zero assembly.
OPTION 2 — PRIME BITES BROWNIE BOWL (~300 CAL / 25-30G PROTEIN): Unwrap 1 Prime Bites protein brownie and place it in a small dessert bowl. Any flavor works.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop 1/4 Pint Ice Cream on Top
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1/4 pint of lighter or high-protein ice cream — Halo Top and Frozen One are both examples. Halo Top and Frozen One are average on their own; paired with the brownie, the full dessert becomes an easy 8/10.

recipeInstructions.name: Eat Immediately
recipeInstructions.text: The ice cream starts softening into the brownie within 30-60 seconds. The pairing IS the fix — two average products become one real dessert.

recipe.name: High-Protein Caesar Dressing
recipe.description: Sauce Series Ep. 6. Blender Caesar that adds protein instead of fat — about 30 cal and 3g protein per 2 tbsp.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend
recipeInstructions.text: Add every ingredient to a high-speed blender.

recipeInstructions.name: Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Blend until completely smooth — give the cottage cheese the full run so no curds remain.

recipeInstructions.name: Measure + Store
recipeInstructions.text: Measure the finished yield, refrigerate in a sealed container, and stir before serving.

recipe.name: High-Protein Cheesecake Fudgy Bars
recipe.description: Inspired by Nora's fudgy bars, rebuilt Split Plate. 8 bars across 2 containers, 170 cal / 15g protein each, three cold layers.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix The Fudge Base
recipeInstructions.text: Stir the almond flour, black cocoa, sugar-free maple syrup, Fairlife whole milk, and vanilla into a thick, fudgy dough. It should hold together like brownie batter that's been chilling — scoopable, not pourable.

recipeInstructions.name: Press Into Two Containers + Freeze 1 hr
recipeInstructions.text: Divide the base between two parchment-lined containers and press into even, firm bases (a flat-bottomed glass helps pack it down). Freeze 1 hour. Packing it firm here is what lets the bars cut clean later.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend The Cheesecake Center — no Coffee
recipeInstructions.text: Blend the cottage cheese ALONE first until completely silky (no surviving curds). Then add the Greek yogurt, Neufchâtel (in chunks), whey-casein, and allulose+monk. Blend thick and smooth. This is the protein-tiramisu cream with an extra ounce of cream cheese and zero coffee — it reads as pure cheesecake here.

recipeInstructions.name: Spread The Cream + Freeze 1 hr
recipeInstructions.text: Divide the cheesecake cream over the two frozen bases and spread even. Freeze another 1 hour so the center firms up before the topping goes on — otherwise the warm topping melts a groove into it.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix The Fudgy Topping
recipeInstructions.text: Stir the unsweetened cocoa and sugar-free maple syrup until glossy and smooth. Equal parts — it thickens into a spreadable fudge as you stir.

recipeInstructions.name: Spread The Topping
recipeInstructions.text: Spread the fudgy topping over both set cheesecake layers in an even coat. Work quickly and gently so you don't drag the cream up into it.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze 1 Final Hr, Cut + Serve Cold
recipeInstructions.text: Freeze one last hour. Cut into 8 bars total across the two containers. Serve fridge-cold, NOT frozen solid — let them sit a few minutes out of the freezer so the cheesecake center goes creamy between the two fudgy layers.

recipe.name: High-Protein Chili Cheese Toast
recipe.description: 8 open-faced toasts. 130 cal / 13g protein each. Blended cottage cheese + reduced-fat fiesta + chilies on keto buns.
recipeIngredient: 4 Oroweat Superior Keto Buns, split into 8 open-faced halves
1 Daisy Low Fat Cottage Cheese cup (5.3 oz / 150g, blended smooth)
1 bag (7 oz / 198g) Great Value Reduced Fat Fiesta Blend shredded cheese
2-4 Thai bird chilies (HOT) OR 1-2 jalapeños (medium heat — remove seeds for milder), finely chopped
Parchment paper or cooking spray (for the baking sheet)

recipeInstructions.name: Oven
recipeInstructions.text: 375°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper (or hit it with cooking spray).

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Cottage Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Daisy Low Fat cup into a small food processor. Blend 30-45 sec until completely smooth — no curds visible. This is the move that makes the filling creamy not chunky.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop to Bowl
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer the blended cottage cheese to a mixing bowl. Should look like thick Greek yogurt at this point.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Full 7 oz bag of Great Value Reduced Fat Fiesta Blend shredded cheese into the bowl with the blended cottage cheese.

recipeInstructions.name: Fold
recipeInstructions.text: Mix the shredded cheese into the cottage-cheese base with a spatula until evenly distributed. Filling should look uniform — no dry shred patches, no cottage-cheese clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Chop Chilies
recipeInstructions.text: 2-4 Thai bird chilies (hot version) OR 1-2 jalapeños with seeds removed (medium version) finely diced — pieces ~1/8-inch. Smaller dice = better distribution across all 8 toasts.

recipeInstructions.name: Fold Chilies Into Filling
recipeInstructions.text: Diced chilies into the cheese mixture. Fold gently to distribute. Don't overmix — visible chili specks throughout the filling is the goal.

recipeInstructions.name: Split Buns
recipeInstructions.text: 4 Oroweat Superior Keto Buns split horizontally into 8 open-faced halves. Arrange cut-side up on the lined baking sheet, spaced so the edges don't touch.

recipeInstructions.name: Fill The Toasts
recipeInstructions.text: Divide the filling evenly across all 8 halves. ~2 tbsp filling per toast. Spread to the edges so the cheese melts to the crust. Pile slightly mounded in the center.

recipeInstructions.name: Season The Tops
recipeInstructions.text: Dan-O's Crunchy Seasoning over each toast. Don't be shy — it's the salt + texture finish. ~1/4 tsp per toast.

recipeInstructions.name: Bake
recipeInstructions.text: 375°F for ~9 min. Filling should be hot + visibly melted + slightly browned on top. Keto buns dry out fast past 10 min — set a timer.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Let toasts cool 1-2 min before eating (cheese filling is molten right out of the oven). Eat 2-3 immediately, reheat the rest later.

recipe.name: High-Protein Chipotle Cheddar Sauce
recipe.description: 70 cal / 8g protein per 1/4 batch. Cottage cheese + cheddar powder + nutritional yeast, blended smooth. Adds Smoky Chipotle Crema for heat.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp Smoky Chipotle Crema (optional — for the adult / heat version)

recipeInstructions.name: Load The Blender
recipeInstructions.text: Cottage cheese + nutritional yeast + cheddar powder + ultra-filtered milk into a small blender or food processor.

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Milk
recipeInstructions.text: 6 tbsp fat-free ultra-filtered milk. Fairlife is shown; any fat-free ultra-filtered milk works.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Cheddar Powder + Nutritional Yeast
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tbsp each. Both carry the cheese flavor — nutritional yeast adds savory depth, cheddar powder adds color and cheddar identity.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Blend until completely smooth, stopping once to scrape the sides if needed.

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Heat (adult Version)
recipeInstructions.text: Blend in 2 tbsp Smoky Chipotle Crema. Omit for the mild base.

recipeInstructions.name: Transfer + Adjust
recipeInstructions.text: Move to a jar. For a thinner drizzle, blend in ultra-filtered milk one teaspoon at a time — added milk shifts yield and macros slightly.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve or Warm Gently
recipeInstructions.text: Use at room temperature, or warm in short 15-second microwave intervals stirring between each. Do not boil — high heat breaks the emulsion.

recipe.name: High-Protein Chipotle-Style Queso
recipe.description: Sauce Series Ep. 5. Baked protein queso — cottage cheese does the creamy work, jalapeños do the kick. About 80 cal and 8g protein per serving.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 tbsp Hoosier Hill Farm cheddar cheese powder

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Blend the MULU cottage cheese with the Fairlife milk until completely smooth — an immersion blender straight in the tub works. Give the cottage cheese the full run so no curds remain.

recipeInstructions.name: Combine
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the smooth base into an oven-safe glass dish. Stir in the nutritional yeast and cheddar powder, lay the sliced Velveeta on top, and scatter the chopped jalapeños over it.

recipeInstructions.name: Bake
recipeInstructions.text: Bake at 300°F for about 15 minutes, until the Velveeta has melted into the base.

recipeInstructions.name: Whisk + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Whisk everything smooth and serve warm.

recipe.name: High-Protein Cilantro Jalapeño Ranch
recipe.description: The viral green sauce from @eatingwithahbaddie, proteinized. 46g protein in the batch.
recipeIngredient: 15.6g (1 serving) Build the Body protein ranch seasoning
Up to 210g La Costeña pickled jalapeño slices (to taste — the filmed batch used the whole jar)

recipeInstructions.name: Base
recipeInstructions.text: Add cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, milk, and protein ranch seasoning to a high-speed blender.

recipeInstructions.name: Greens
recipeInstructions.text: Add pickled jalapeños to your spice tolerance, then half a bunch of cilantro.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Blend until completely smooth. Don't add extra liquid unless the blender stalls — the cottage cheese thins out considerably once it breaks down.

recipeInstructions.name: Bottle
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer to a squeeze bottle and refrigerate before serving.

recipe.name: 2-Minute Ham & Cream Cheese Protein Bagel
recipe.description: One rushed-morning backup — 250 cal / 35g protein, open-face, 2 min, no heat.
recipeIngredient: 1 Sola Plain Bagel (~110 cal / 15g protein per creator's package)
2 tbsp Philadelphia Original Whipped Cream Cheese (1 tbsp per half)
4 slices 365 Organic Black Forest Uncured Ham (~1.5 label servings; 2 slices per half)
1 Bucked Up Green Apple Protein Soda (adds 100 cal / 25g protein → 350 cal / 60g combined). Adult only.

recipeInstructions.name: Split
recipeInstructions.text: Place both bagel halves cut-side up.

recipeInstructions.name: Spread
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tbsp whipped cream cheese over each half.

recipeInstructions.name: Layer Ham
recipeInstructions.text: Top each half with 2 slices of ham and serve open-faced. No lid — the open-face format is intentional so the fillings stay visible and the whole thing eats in 3 bites per half.

recipe.name: High-Protein Japanese Yogurt Hack
recipe.description: One 5.3 oz vanilla Oikos Pro + six HighKey mini chocolate-chip protein cookies. Press whole, chill overnight, cake-soft cookies-and-cream breakfast. 260 cal / 27g protein.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (5.3 oz / 150 g) vanilla Oikos Pro yogurt — 130 cal / 20g protein on the package used
6 HighKey Chocolate Chip Protein Mini Cookies (~35 g / 1 serving) — 130 cal / 7g protein on the bag used

recipeInstructions.name: Open The Cup
recipeInstructions.text: Open one 5.3 oz vanilla Oikos Pro yogurt. Leave the yogurt in its cup — this stays a one-container breakfast.

recipeInstructions.name: Press Cookies in Whole
recipeInstructions.text: Press all six HighKey chocolate-chip mini cookies straight into the yogurt. Keep them whole — do NOT crush them first. The chill is what softens them.

recipeInstructions.name: Chill 4 hr Minimum (overnight Best)
recipeInstructions.text: Cover and refrigerate. Four hours is the floor. Overnight is the sweet spot — the cookies turn cake-soft, not crunchy, not dissolved.

recipeInstructions.name: Fold Once + Eat Cold
recipeInstructions.text: Give the chilled cup one gentle fold — enough to marble the cookie pieces through, not enough to purée them. Eat straight out of the cup.

recipe.name: High-Protein Muffin Cup Powerup
recipe.description: 285 cal. 35g protein. 17g fiber. Microwave mug cake with cookie-dough chunks. 3 minutes flat.
recipeIngredient: 1 Bootylicious High Protein Muffin Cup (any flavor — Double Chocolate, Cookies & Creme, Cinnamon Bun, Blueberry, Chocolate Peanut Butter, etc.)
1/2 to 3/4 of a Hormbles Chormbles bar, chopped (~75 cal portion)
Optional: extra splash of Fairlife after cooking for softer texture

recipeInstructions.name: Mise
recipeInstructions.text: Pop the Bootylicious cup lid + remove any inner foil seal. Measure 1/4 cup Fairlife. Pull out the Hormbles Chormbles bar + a small cutting board.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Stir
recipeInstructions.text: 1/4 cup Fairlife straight into the Bootylicious cup. Stir with a spoon until the dry mix is fully hydrated — no dry pockets. Batter should be thick like brownie batter, not soupy.

recipeInstructions.name: Chop The Chormbles
recipeInstructions.text: ~75 cal worth of Hormbles Chormbles bar into small chunks (~1/4-inch). That's about 3/4 of the original 100-cal SKU, or 1/2 of the newer 140-cal SKU.

recipeInstructions.name: Fold in
recipeInstructions.text: Sprinkle the chopped Chormbles over the batter. Fold gently with the spoon to distribute. Don't overmix — visible chunks are the point.

recipeInstructions.name: Microwave
recipeInstructions.text: 1 minute on high. If your microwave runs hot, start at 50 sec + add 10-sec bursts. Top should set but center stays slightly soft.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Eat
recipeInstructions.text: 30 sec rest (keeps setting as it cools). Optional Fairlife splash on top for softer texture. Spoon, straight from the cup.

recipe.name: High-Protein Viral Dot Cake
recipe.description: Viral dot cake, protein version. 3 ramekin cakes per batch, 250 cal / 25g protein each (base 170/19 + cheesecake frosting + sprinkles).
recipeIngredient: 2 scoops (62g) PEScience Select Gourmet Vanilla Protein Powder
3 large Happy Egg Co Organic Free-Range Eggs
15g Whole Earth Monk Fruit Erythritol Sweetener Blend
15g Jell-O Sugar-Free Vanilla Instant Pudding Mix (about half a 1 oz box)
1 tsp Clabber Girl Double-Acting Baking Powder
1 serving (30g) Protein Cheesecake Frosting per cake — 60 cal / 6g protein each
Rainbow nonpareil sprinkles, ~5g per cake (~20 cal/cake)

recipeInstructions.name: Preheat
recipeInstructions.text: Oven to 350°F. Spray 3 ramekins (6-8 oz size) with cooking spray.

recipeInstructions.name: Dry Mix
recipeInstructions.text: In a mixing bowl on a scale, combine 62g PEScience Vanilla + 45g AP flour + 15g Whole Earth Monk Fruit Erythritol + 15g Jell-O Sugar-Free Vanilla Pudding Mix + 1 tsp Clabber Girl baking powder. Whisk dry to break up any protein-powder clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Wet Mix
recipeInstructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk 3 eggs + 1/4 cup Fairlife + 1 tsp vanilla extract until uniform.

recipeInstructions.name: Combine
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the wet into the dry. Whisk until smooth — should be thick cake batter that just barely flows off the whisk. Don't overmix; lumps cook out.

recipeInstructions.name: Fill Ramekins
recipeInstructions.text: Divide batter evenly across 3 ramekins. Smooth the tops with a spatula. Ramekins should be ~3/4 full — the cakes rise then settle.

recipeInstructions.name: Bake 350°f × 15 Min
recipeInstructions.text: Tops should be golden + spring back lightly. Centers should still feel SOFT to the touch — the liquidy-molten center is the viral dot cake signature. Past 18 min = dry center = lost moment.

recipeInstructions.name: Cool + Trim
recipeInstructions.text: Let ramekins cool 10 min on a wire rack, then chill in the fridge 30 min (or overnight). Once chilled, slice the domed top off each cake with a serrated knife so the surface is flat for frosting. The trimmed scraps = the 4th serving (snack them, freeze for parfaits, or compost).

recipeInstructions.name: Frost
recipeInstructions.text: Spread one 30g serving of [Protein Cheesecake Frosting](/cookbook/protein-cheesecake-frosting) over each flat-trimmed cake top. Smooth to the edges. Thick frosting holds peaks; thin frosting pools — refer to the parent frosting recipe troubleshooting if it's too thin.

recipeInstructions.name: Sprinkle Dip
recipeInstructions.text: Pour ~5g rainbow nonpareils onto a shallow plate. Press the frosted top of each cake into the sprinkles to coat. Lift gently — frosting holds the sprinkles in place.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop + Eat
recipeInstructions.text: Best within 2 hours of frosting (sprinkle crunch fades after 4-6 hours as moisture migrates). Scoop through the sprinkle top + frosting + cake — molten center reveals itself on the spoon.

recipe.name: Hot Dog Chili Base
recipe.description: 12-serving no-bean beef chili — thick enough to stay on a hot dog. One cook covers a chili dog dinner plus a later chili mac / baked-potato / fries night.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Spiceology Beef-Infused BBQ Rub (or use the alternative seasoning blend below)

recipeInstructions.name: Brown The Beef
recipeInstructions.text: Add 2 lb 93/7 ground beef to a wide hot pan and break into small crumbles as it browns.

recipeInstructions.name: Season
recipeInstructions.text: 3 tbsp Spiceology Beef-Infused BBQ Rub. Or, if using the alternative, add 2 tsp each of paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt. Stir to coat.

recipeInstructions.name: Dijon + Worcestershire
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tbsp Dijon mustard + 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce. Stir into the beef.

recipeInstructions.name: Tomato Paste
recipeInstructions.text: 6 oz. Stir until the paste coats the beef evenly.

recipeInstructions.name: Bone Broth
recipeInstructions.text: 1 cup chicken bone broth. Combine thoroughly.

recipeInstructions.name: Reduce
recipeInstructions.text: Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the visible liquid is gone and the chili is thick and spoonable. Taste. Add salt only if needed — the rub already carries salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Divide
recipeInstructions.text: 12 equal servings. Use 1 serving per hot dog. Refrigerate or freeze the rest promptly (within 2 hours per USDA leftovers guidance).

recipe.name: Hot Honey Mustard Crispy Chicken Tacos
recipe.description: Three crispy chicken tacos with creamy Caesar and sweet heat. About 510 calories and 44g protein for all three with optional chilies.
recipeIngredient: 6 oz Realgood lightly breaded chicken fillets, weighed frozen; divide the heated batch equally among three tacos
3 La Banderita Carb Counter Street Taco tortillas (avocado-oil 14-count pack shown)
1 tbsp homemade high-protein Caesar dressing (1 tsp per taco); another sauce changes the nutrition
1½ tbsp Trader Joe’s Hot Honey Mustard condiment (½ tbsp per taco; not the refrigerated dressing)
Optional: 1 tbsp DeLallo chopped Calabrian chilies (1 tsp per taco)

recipeInstructions.name: Cook The Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the fillets according to the directions on the actual package. The footage begins with cooked chicken; no creator-specific time or temperature was supplied.

recipeInstructions.name: Lay Out The Tortillas
recipeInstructions.text: Set out the three La Banderita street taco tortillas.

recipeInstructions.name: Slice The Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: Slice the cooked fillets into strips.

recipeInstructions.name: Spread Caesar
recipeInstructions.text: Spread 1 teaspoon of protein Caesar on each tortilla, then divide the cooked chicken from the 6 oz frozen-weight batch evenly among the three tacos. Each gets a 2 oz pre-heating weight equivalent.

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle Mustard
recipeInstructions.text: Add ½ tablespoon Trader Joe’s Hot Honey Mustard to each taco.

recipeInstructions.name: Optional Chili + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Add up to 1 teaspoon chopped Calabrian chilies to each taco if desired. Fold and serve.

recipe.name: Hot Honey Mustard Hack Sauce
recipe.description: 2 ingredients. 60 seconds. Money Mustard's lazy cousin.

recipeInstructions.name: Bowl
recipeInstructions.text: 30g French's yellow mustard into a small dipping bowl or ramekin.

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle
recipeInstructions.text: 10g ChocZero Keto Hot Honey on top of the mustard.

recipeInstructions.name: Stir
recipeInstructions.text: Whisk or stir with a fork until fully smooth and glossy — no streaks of honey on top, no mustard pockets at the bottom. Should be the texture of warm honey mustard, not paste.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Straight into the dip. Best with air-fryer chicken nuggets, chicken tenders, breaded chicken chunks, or roasted potatoes. Eat immediately — this is a fresh-make sauce, not a meal-prep batch.

recipe.name: Indo-Chinese Chili Sauce
recipe.description: 6 ingredients. 1 glass. Restaurant-level glaze.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Kikkoman Thai Style Chili Sauce

recipeInstructions.name: Mix
recipeInstructions.text: Combine all 6 ingredients in a glass. Stir.

recipeInstructions.name: Use
recipeInstructions.text: Pour ALL at once into a hot wok with cooked veg. Boil hard 60-90 sec until glossy and reduced.

recipeInstructions.name: Coat
recipeInstructions.text: Add crispy protein, toss 45-75 seconds. Kill heat immediately.

recipe.name: Key Lime Cheesecake Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 2, Flavor 3 — green protein Creami with 2 tsp lime gelatin mix in the base, 15g frozen Protein Cheesecake Frosting Respun through the pint, crisp graham finish. ~350 cal / 42g protein whole pint. First cross-recipe Creami — chains to the existing Protein Cheesecake Frosting cookbook entry.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
2 level tsp regular lime gelatin dessert mix (~7-8g, ~30 cal — see substitutions for halal/pork-free notes)
15g frozen Protein Cheesecake Frosting, chopped small (~30 cal) — use the cookbook recipe
60 cal graham crackers, crushed (roughly 1 sheet Honey Maid or equivalent)

recipeInstructions.name: Pour Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk to a Creami pint (or blending vessel).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sweetener
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Whey Isolate
recipeInstructions.text: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Guar Gum
recipeInstructions.text: 1/8 tsp guar gum, LEVEL measure. Heaped = gummy.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Salt
recipeInstructions.text: 1 pinch salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Lime Gelatin Mix
recipeInstructions.text: 2 LEVEL teaspoons regular lime gelatin dessert mix (about 7-8g, ~30 cal). This is the flavor carrier — 2 level tsp is the right dose. More reads too tart; less doesn't land as Key Lime. Verify package for halal/pork-free suitability (gelatin source often unspecified — see substitutions).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Green Color
recipeInstructions.text: 5 drops green food coloring. Distributed pre-blend so the finished base is uniformly green.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Immersion blender until completely smooth and evenly green. Zero lumps, zero visible whey, uniform color. The lime gelatin dissolves fully into the base at this stage.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer to a Creami pint if you didn't build in the pint. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest 5 Min + First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes — NO hot-water bath. Process on Regular Ice Cream, NOT Lite. The first spin may look powdery; expected because the Respin (with frozen frosting) finishes the texture.

recipeInstructions.name: Chop Frozen Frosting
recipeInstructions.text: Take 15g of the pre-frozen Protein Cheesecake Frosting (from `/cookbook/protein-cheesecake-frosting`) and chop it into small pieces (~1/4 inch cubes). Pieces must be frozen solid or they'll blend into the base rather than holding as pockets.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Frozen Frosting
recipeInstructions.text: Poke the frozen frosting pieces into the surface of the first-spin pint. Distributes better when pushed in rather than piled on top.

recipeInstructions.name: Respin
recipeInstructions.text: Run one Respin cycle. Respin serves double duty here: distributes the cheesecake pockets through the pint AND finishes the powdery texture from the first spin. Same technique family as W2F2 Beach Bum (which Respun a graham cracker) — different mix-in.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the finished pint into a bowl. Green Creami with visible cheesecake pockets pulled through.

recipeInstructions.name: Graham Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Crush ~60 cal graham crackers (roughly 1 sheet Honey Maid or equivalent) over the scoops. Serve immediately — graham softens fast on ice cream.

recipe.name: Lean Beef Meatballs (30-piece Base)
recipe.description: The batch component. 30 lean beef meatballs from 2 lb of 93/7, oven-baked 10-13 min at 425°F. 5 meatballs = 285 cal / 34g protein. Feeds Meatball Parm Puff, pizza night, pasta, sandwiches, red-sauce bowls.
recipeIngredient: Salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Preheat Oven 425°f
recipeInstructions.text: Line a sheet pan with parchment or foil.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix Gently
recipeInstructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Mix just until combined — DO NOT overwork the beef. Overworking makes tough meatballs.

recipeInstructions.name: Portion 30
recipeInstructions.text: Divide the mixture into 30 meatballs (about 30 g each). A cookie scoop keeps them uniform. Arrange on the sheet pan with space between so they brown, not steam.

recipeInstructions.name: Bake 10-13 Min
recipeInstructions.text: Until the centers reach 160°F on an instant-read thermometer. Timing depends on ball size — pull at 160°F, not by clock.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Store
recipeInstructions.text: Let rest 3-4 min before serving. For meal prep, cool completely before boxing so condensation doesn't turn the outsides mushy.

recipe.name: 10-Minute Leftover Beef Kebab Tacos
recipe.description: 10-min street taco lunch built from 3 leftover Costco beef kebabs. Chain-cook from Freezer Shortcut Beef Kebab Pitas (id 54).
recipeIngredient: 3 fully cooked Mediterranean beef kebabs (The Falafel Company at Costco — verify halal on the current physical package)
3 low-carb street taco flour tortillas (La Banderita Carb Counter shown)
3 tsp Tari hot sauce, optional (~1 tsp per taco, any preferred flavor)

recipeInstructions.name: Thaw
recipeInstructions.text: Thaw the fully cooked beef kebabs overnight in the refrigerator.

recipeInstructions.name: Air-fry
recipeInstructions.text: Reheat kebabs 7-8 min at the temperature on the current package, until thoroughly hot. Physical package directions take priority.

recipeInstructions.name: Warm Tortillas
recipeInstructions.text: Warm the 3 street tortillas per package directions (or skip if you like them cold).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Kebabs
recipeInstructions.text: Place one reheated kebab on each tortilla.

recipeInstructions.name: Pickled Onion
recipeInstructions.text: Top each taco with pickled red onions.

recipeInstructions.name: Tari Drizzle (optional)
recipeInstructions.text: Finish with ~1 tsp Tari hot sauce per taco, or skip the sauce. Serve immediately.

recipe.name: Leftover Cheeseburger Tacos
recipe.description: 10-min cheeseburger taco lunch built from 4 oz of leftover 93/7 ground beef. Chain-cook from Smash Burger Night (id 47).
recipeIngredient: 2 low-carb street taco tortillas (La Banderita Carb Counter shown)
4 oz 93/7 ground beef (leftover from Smash Burger Night is ideal)
1 Velveeta Original slice (split in half — 1/2 per taco)
Avocado oil spray (Chosen Foods or similar)
Salt or burger seasoning, to taste
Sauce drizzle to taste (burger sauce, hot sauce, mustard sauce, or house drizzle)
Pickled red onion, to taste (adds crunch + acidity)

recipeInstructions.name: Tortillas
recipeInstructions.text: Lay out 2 low-carb street taco tortillas on the counter.

recipeInstructions.name: Portion Beef
recipeInstructions.text: Divide 4 oz 93/7 ground beef across the tortillas — about 2 oz per tortilla.

recipeInstructions.name: Smash Thin
recipeInstructions.text: Press the beef thin across each tortilla so it cooks like a smash-burger taco. Get right to the tortilla edges.

recipeInstructions.name: Season
recipeInstructions.text: Salt or burger seasoning across the smashed beef side.

recipeInstructions.name: Cook Beef-down
recipeInstructions.text: Heat a pan or griddle on medium-high, avocado oil spray. Place tacos beef-side down and cook 2-3 min until the beef browns and the tortilla starts to crisp.

recipeInstructions.name: Flip + Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Flip both tacos. Add 1/2 Velveeta slice on each. Let the cheese soften ~30 sec.

recipeInstructions.name: Pickled Onion
recipeInstructions.text: Scatter pickled red onion across the cheese side while everything's still hot.

recipeInstructions.name: Sauce + Fold
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle sauce to taste. Fold each taco and crisp both folded sides briefly in the pan for texture.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve Hot
recipeInstructions.text: The texture is the point — crisp tortilla, melty cheese, tangy onion. Eat immediately.

recipe.name: Lift Drizzle
recipe.description: Five ingredients. Bright + salty + fermented + hot. Acid does the lift.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp olive oil (California Organic Extra Virgin, or any quality EVOO)
3 tbsp ReaLemon lemon juice (~6 portions, or fresh-squeezed from 1 lemon)
2 fresh red Thai chilies, finely chopped

recipeInstructions.name: Whisk in a Small Bowl
recipeInstructions.text: Olive oil + soy sauce + fish sauce + lemon juice + coriander powder. Whisk until the coriander dissolves (it tries to clump — keep whisking).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Chilies
recipeInstructions.text: Chop 2 fresh red Thai chilies finely. Stir in. The chili oil + capsaicin needs to mingle for ~2 min before serving — they're not just visual.

recipeInstructions.name: Taste + Adjust
recipeInstructions.text: Too salty → bump lemon by 1 tsp. Too flat → add 1 more pinch coriander. Too thin / runny — DON'T thicken with cornstarch (that's the takeout trap). Add 1 more tsp olive oil if you want body, but flat-and-bright is the brand.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Small bowl with a small spoon. Adults spoon into their wraps / bowls / salads at the table. Never pour over the platter — lettuce wilts in 60 sec.

recipe.name: Loaded Steak & Egg Skillet
recipe.description: Same meal. Different plates. Everyone wins.
recipeIngredient: 3 oz Soules Kitchen Thinly Sliced Beef Fajitas
1 oz Kraft Fat Free Cheddar Cheese
Fresh red + green chilies (optional — adults only)

recipeInstructions.name: Prep
recipeInstructions.text: Chop Soules fajita beef into smaller pieces if needed. Slice chilies. Whisk eggs with a pinch of Redmond Real Salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Heat + Build
recipeInstructions.text: Medium heat pan. Add steak + chilies. Season with Dan-O's Crunchy. Cook 1–2 min — it's already cooked, just reheat + slight crisp.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Eggs
recipeInstructions.text: Pour eggs evenly over steak. Do not stir. Cover the pan — this is key.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Sprinkle 1 oz Kraft fat-free cheddar evenly. Light hit of Dan-O's Crunchy on top.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Cover 1–2 min until eggs are set. Fold or leave open-face.

recipe.name: Mallow Sandwich Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 3, Flavor 1 — black-cocoa protein Creami pint, protein-brownie Respin, and a post-scoop marshmallow ribbon. ~370 cal / 48g protein whole pint vs 970 cal for the Crumbl Mallow Sandwich Cookie ft. OREO on the current Crumbl UT/American Fork nutrition listing.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1/3 of a Prime Bites Cookie Monster protein brownie, cut small (~75 cal)
1/2 tbsp Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk (to loosen the creme)

recipeInstructions.name: Pour Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk to a Creami pint (or blending vessel).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sweetener
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Whey Isolate
recipeInstructions.text: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Guar Gum
recipeInstructions.text: 1/8 tsp guar gum, LEVEL measure. Heaped = gummy.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Salt
recipeInstructions.text: 1 pinch salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Black Cocoa
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tbsp black cocoa powder. Black cocoa (Dutch-processed, extra-dark) is the OREO-adjacent flavor carrier — regular cocoa reads as milk chocolate, black cocoa reads as bittersweet sandwich-cookie chocolate. Series-first: no prior CCC episode used black cocoa.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Immersion blender until completely smooth and evenly dark. Zero lumps, zero visible whey, uniform deep-brown-to-near-black color from the black cocoa.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer to a Creami pint if you didn't build in the pint. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours. Do not exceed the max-fill line.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest 5 Min + First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes — NO hot-water bath. Process on Regular Ice Cream, NOT Lite. The first spin may look grainy; expected because the Respin (with brownie pieces) finishes the texture.

recipeInstructions.name: Cut Brownie
recipeInstructions.text: Cut 1/3 of a Prime Bites Cookie Monster protein brownie into small pieces (~1/4 inch cubes). ~75 cal of brownie is the target — verify the current package weight and adjust the portion if the brownie size has changed.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Brownie + Respin
recipeInstructions.text: Poke the brownie pieces into the surface of the first-spin pint (better distribution than piling on top). Run one Respin cycle. Respin distributes the brownie pieces AND finishes the grainy texture from the first spin. Same technique family as W2F2 Beach Bum and W2F3 Key Lime — different mix-in.

recipeInstructions.name: Respin Result
recipeInstructions.text: The finished Respin should show visible brownie pieces distributed through the pint with a smooth, non-grainy Creami texture. If the texture still reads powdery, run a second Respin.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the finished pint into a bowl. Deep-dark chocolate Creami with visible brownie pockets pulled through.

recipeInstructions.name: Loosen Marshmallow Creme
recipeInstructions.text: In a small bowl, add 2 tbsp marshmallow creme + 1/2 tbsp Fairlife 2% milk. Stir until glossy and pourable — this converts stiff marshmallow creme into a ribbon consistency without cooking or heating. The 1/2 tbsp milk is the exact ratio; more will thin it too much.

recipeInstructions.name: Stir to Ribbon
recipeInstructions.text: Continue stirring until the marshmallow-and-milk mixture is uniformly glossy with no dry pockets. Should pour off the spoon in a slow ribbon, not a fast drizzle.

recipeInstructions.name: Ribbon + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle the marshmallow ribbon over the scoops. The ribbon is a POST-SCOOP GARNISH — not a machine mix-in. Adding marshmallow to the pint before Respin turns the whole pint gummy; keeping it as a final drizzle preserves the ice-cream texture underneath and the glossy marshmallow filling identity on top. Serve immediately — marshmallow starts to firm back up as it cools.

recipe.name: Maple Waffle Brunch Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 11 — breakfast-inspired kid snack box: boiled egg, 365 uncured Black Forest ham, St Pierre Belgian waffle with Kirkland organic maple syrup, fresh strawberries. ~250 cal / 14g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 4 hard-boiled eggs — 1 peeled, halved egg per box
4.8 oz 365 Whole Foods Uncured Organic Black Forest Ham — 1.2 oz per box
2 St Pierre Belgian Waffles — 1/2 waffle per box, cut into bite-size pieces, no added butter
2 tbsp Kirkland Signature Organic Maple Syrup — 1/2 tbsp drizzled per box
Fresh strawberries — hulled and cut to fill each box
Optional: light seasoning for the eggs (family's preferred blend)

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Line up 4 divided snack boxes. Buluker pastel 4-compartment boxes shown — the same set featured on Favorites → Snack Box Essentials.

recipeInstructions.name: Boiled Eggs
recipeInstructions.text: Peel and halve 4 hard-boiled eggs. Place 1 halved egg (both halves) in one compartment of each box. Light seasoning if desired — the family's preferred egg seasoning.

recipeInstructions.name: Ham
recipeInstructions.text: Fold or cut 1.2 oz of 365 Black Forest uncured ham into one compartment of each box (~4.8 oz total across all 4 boxes).

recipeInstructions.name: Waffle
recipeInstructions.text: Cut 2 St Pierre Belgian waffles into bite-size pieces. Divide evenly across all 4 boxes — half a waffle per box. No added butter — the maple syrup drizzle carries the fat + flavor.

recipeInstructions.name: Maple Syrup
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle 1/2 tablespoon Kirkland organic maple syrup over the waffle pieces in each box. Measure — free-pouring blows the calorie budget past 250. If the family prefers a firmer waffle, drizzle closer to serving instead of packing time.

recipeInstructions.name: Strawberries
recipeInstructions.text: Hull and cut fresh strawberries into kid-friendly bite pieces. Fill the remaining compartment of each box.

recipeInstructions.name: Seal + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lids on and refrigerate. Serve within 2 days. Transport with an ice pack for lunchbox use.

recipe.name: Marbled Stuffed Cheesecake Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 1, Flavor 1 — two-freeze marbled chocolate + vanilla protein Creami pint, stuffed with frozen cheesecake frosting + Lily's chips + Teddy Graham finish. 335 cal / 45g protein whole pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
15g Protein Cheesecake Frosting (~1/2 serving; freeze firm and chop — cross-recipe /cookbook/protein-cheesecake-frosting)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt. Immersion blender until completely smooth. Zero lumps — Creami texture depends on this.

recipeInstructions.name: Split + Chocolate Half
recipeInstructions.text: Divide the base evenly into two portions. Blend 1/2 tbsp black cocoa into ONE half. Keep the vanilla half in a covered container.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze #1 (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the chocolate half into a level Creami pint. Freeze upright for 24 hours. Keep the reserved vanilla half covered + refrigerated during this window.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze #2 (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the vanilla half OVER the fully-frozen chocolate layer. Freeze upright for another 24 hours. Two layers, two freezes — this is the marbling technique.

recipeInstructions.name: Prep Frosting
recipeInstructions.text: While the pint finishes freezing, freeze 15g [Protein Cheesecake Frosting](/cookbook/protein-cheesecake-frosting) until firm (~30 min in the freezer). Chop into small mix-in pieces.

recipeInstructions.name: Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Briefly run warm water over the OUTSIDE of the frozen pint to release the layers. Process on Regular Ice Cream (NOT Lite). Use Respin if the first spin comes out powdery.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in
recipeInstructions.text: Make a narrow center well in the spun ice cream. Drop in the chopped frozen frosting pieces + 7g Lily's chips. Run the Mix-In cycle.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop into a bowl. Top with 7g crushed Teddy Grahams — added AFTER all machine cycles so they stay crisp. Eat immediately.

recipe.name: Mexican Lavash Pizza
recipe.description: Quick Lunches Ep. 8 — crisp lavash pizza, 450°F for 8 min. ~290 cal / 31g protein per half (585 / 62 whole). Joseph's lavash + Trader Joe's spicy red sauce + two cheeses + Kirkland chipotle chicken.
recipeIngredient: 1 Joseph's flax, oat bran & whole wheat lavash (120 cal / 12g protein per flatbread)
1/4 cup (1 serving) Trader Joe's Thick, Bold & Spicy Red Sauce (100 cal / 1g protein)
1.5 oz reduced-fat shredded mozzarella (calc assumes ~70 cal / 8g protein per oz)
6 oz Kirkland Signature chipotle chicken, fully cooked (200 cal / 32g protein)
1 oz Velveeta Original shreds (60 cal / 5g protein)

recipeInstructions.name: Heat + Place
recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oven to 450°F and place the lavash on a parchment-lined sheet pan.

recipeInstructions.name: Sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Spread the red sauce across the lavash, leaving a narrow border.

recipeInstructions.name: Cheese + Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: Add the reduced-fat mozzarella, distribute the chopped chipotle chicken evenly, then finish with the Velveeta shreds.

recipeInstructions.name: Bake
recipeInstructions.text: Bake 8 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the lavash edges are crisp.

recipeInstructions.name: Slice + Store
recipeInstructions.text: Cut into two equal servings. Eat immediately, or refrigerate the second half for tomorrow — it also eats well cold.

recipe.name: Midnight Mix Creami
recipe.description: Chocolate protein ice cream with the 5g mix-in method.
recipeIngredient: 1/8 tsp Bob's Red Mill Guar Gum

recipeInstructions.name: Blend
recipeInstructions.text: Add all base ingredients to Creami pint. Immersion blender until completely smooth. No clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Freeze flat for 12-16 hours. Uneven freeze = bad texture.

recipeInstructions.name: First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Select Lite Ice Cream or Regular Ice Cream.

recipeInstructions.name: Fix Texture
recipeInstructions.text: If powdery, re-spin — NO extra milk. Adding milk here ruins it.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in
recipeInstructions.text: Create a center well. Add all 4 mix-ins (5g each). Run Mix-In mode.

recipeInstructions.name: Eat
recipeInstructions.text: Immediately. Don't refreeze.

recipe.name: Midnight S'mores Protein Creami
recipe.description: Chocolate Creami with graham, marshmallow creme, and chocolate drizzle. About 375 calories and 43g protein for the whole finished pint.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 graham-cracker sheet, 1 tbsp marshmallow creme, and about 1 tbsp zero-sugar chocolate syrup

recipeInstructions.name: Blend
recipeInstructions.text: Blend the shared base with 1 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa until fully smooth. These amounts make one pint.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into one Creami pint below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Rest about five minutes, then run Regular Ice Cream. If powdery, run a no-liquid Respin before mix-ins.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in
recipeInstructions.text: Break one full graham-cracker sheet into the spun pint and run Mix-In.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop; add half a graham sheet, 1 tbsp marshmallow creme, and about 1 tbsp zero-sugar chocolate syrup. Serve immediately.

recipe.name: Minecraft Cherry Blossom Cookie Creami
recipe.description: Cherry protein Creami inspired by Crumbl's Minecraft Cherry Blossom Cookie — maraschino cherries blended through the pink pint, mini vanilla wafers split between mix-in and topping, and one cherry on top. 390 calories and 42g protein for the complete pint.
recipeIngredient: Maraschino cherries, to taste (blended in; exact quantity not measured on camera)
1/2 serving mini vanilla wafers (mix-in, after the first spin)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend The Cherry Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine the usual base — 2% ultra-filtered milk, unflavored whey isolate, vanilla, monk fruit, guar gum, and salt — with maraschino cherries to taste. Blend until completely smooth and pink with no whey clumps. The exact cherry quantity was not measured on camera; add to taste for color and flavor.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour, Freeze + First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint without exceeding the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level overnight, then process on Regular Ice Cream. If it stays powdery, run one no-liquid Respin.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix in Wafers
recipeInstructions.text: Cut a center well, add half of a 150-calorie serving of mini vanilla wafers, and run Mix-In.

recipeInstructions.name: Top With Wafers
recipeInstructions.text: Crumble the remaining half serving of mini vanilla wafers over the top.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish With a Cherry
recipeInstructions.text: Top with one maraschino cherry and eat immediately for the intended soft-serve texture.

recipe.name: Minecraft Cookie Butter Cookie Creami
recipe.description: Cookie-butter protein Creami inspired by Crumbl's Minecraft Cookie Butter Cookie — Biscoff spread blended through the pint, plus two Lotus cookies split between mix-in and topping. 370 calories and 41g protein for the complete pint.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine the 2% ultra-filtered milk, whey isolate, vanilla, monk fruit, guar gum, salt, 1/2 tsp cookie butter emulsion, and 1 tsp Biscoff cookie butter. Blend until completely smooth with no whey clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint without exceeding the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level overnight.

recipeInstructions.name: First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Process the frozen pint on Regular Ice Cream. If it stays powdery, run one no-liquid Respin before adding mix-ins.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Mix-ins
recipeInstructions.text: Cut a center well and add 1 tsp Biscoff cookie butter and one Lotus Biscoff cookie, then run Mix-In. Note that the mixed-in cookie loses most of its crunch.

recipeInstructions.name: Top + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Crumble the second Lotus Biscoff cookie over the top and eat immediately for the intended texture. For stronger crunch, keep both cookies on top instead of mixing one in.

recipe.name: Minecraft Cookies & Cream Sandwich Cookie Creami
recipe.description: Chocolate cookies-and-cream protein Creami with brownie and sandwich-cookie mix-ins and a purple marshmallow-creme finish. 385 calories and 46g protein for the complete pint.
recipeIngredient: Natural red and blue food coloring, as needed

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine the 2% ultra-filtered milk, whey isolate, black cocoa, vanilla, monk fruit, guar gum, and salt. Blend until completely smooth with no cocoa or whey clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint without exceeding the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level overnight.

recipeInstructions.name: First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Process the frozen pint on Regular Ice Cream. If it stays powdery, run one no-liquid Respin before adding mix-ins.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Mix-ins
recipeInstructions.text: Cut a center well and add one-third of the Cookie Monster brownie and one chocolate sandwich cookie, then run Mix-In.

recipeInstructions.name: Make Purple Creme
recipeInstructions.text: Stir natural red and blue food coloring into 2 tablespoons of marshmallow creme until it turns an even purple.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop + Drizzle
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the Creami into a bowl and drizzle the purple marshmallow creme over the top. Eat immediately for the intended texture.

recipe.name: Mississippi Mud Pie Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 6, Flavor 1 (Ep. 16 / Week 6 opener) — darkest Creami in the series so far: 2 tbsp Dutch cocoa in the base, cocoa grahams through Respin, Mid-Day Squares brownie garnish + sugar-free whipped cream + cocoa dusting on top. 390 cal / 46g protein whole pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
2 tbsp Dutch cocoa (intentionally dark — the darkest cocoa dose in the series so far)
1/3 square chocolate brownie (Mid-Day Squares filmed) — chopped, garnish only
Dutch cocoa, as needed for a light dusting

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt + 2 tbsp Dutch cocoa. Immersion blender until completely smooth. Zero cocoa lumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes. Process on Regular Ice Cream. First-spin texture is expected to look dark and slightly powdery — the Respin fixes it.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in Cocoa Grahams
recipeInstructions.text: Make a narrow center well. Drop in 0.5 oz (14g) of cocoa grahams (Crazy Grahams filmed). Run RESPIN without adding liquid — this is the crunchy cookie element.

recipeInstructions.name: Respin Result
recipeInstructions.text: Post-Respin should read as a dark, smooth, cocoa-graham-flecked pint. If it's still powdery, add nothing and Respin one more time.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop into a bowl. Reserve the pint for the finish — brownie + whipped cream + cocoa go on top of the scooped Creami, not the pint.

recipeInstructions.name: Chop Brownie
recipeInstructions.text: Chop 1/3 of a Mid-Day Squares chocolate brownie into rustic bite-sized pieces. Garnish only — the brownie does NOT go through the machine.

recipeInstructions.name: Garnish + Whip + Dust
recipeInstructions.text: Scatter the chopped brownie over the scoop. Add 1 tbsp sugar-free whipped cream. Light Dutch cocoa dusting on top for the mud-pie finish. Eat immediately — the cocoa-graham crunch is best in the first 2-3 minutes.

recipe.name: No-Dish Protein Ramen
recipe.description: ~34g protein. 7 minutes. Zero dishes. Eat from the container.
recipeIngredient: 1 Miyoka Protein Spicy Ramen container (25g protein)
1 cup Kirkland Chicken Bone Broth (not water — 9g extra protein)

recipeInstructions.name: Cook
recipeInstructions.text: Add noodles to a small pot. Pour in 1 cup bone broth. Boil, then reduce to medium. Cook 5-7 min until soft and broth is mostly absorbed.

recipeInstructions.name: Transfer
recipeInstructions.text: Pour cooked noodles back into the Miyoka container. No bowl needed.

recipeInstructions.name: Sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Add the sauce packet. Close lid. Shake well. Let sit 1-2 min to coat.

recipeInstructions.name: Eat
recipeInstructions.text: Directly from the container. Done.

recipe.name: Mocha Brownie Protein Creami
recipe.description: Coffee-forward decaf protein ice cream with Brownie Brittle crunch. 345 calories and 42g protein for the complete pint.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine the 2% ultra-filtered milk, whey isolate, decaf instant coffee, monk fruit, guar gum, and salt. Blend until completely smooth with no coffee or whey clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint without exceeding the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for at least 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Let the frozen pint rest at room temperature for 5 minutes. Process using Regular Ice Cream.

recipeInstructions.name: Check Texture
recipeInstructions.text: If the first spin remains powdery, run one no-liquid Respin. Do not automatically add milk.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Brownie Brittle
recipeInstructions.text: Cut a narrow center well and add 2/3 serving of chocolate-chip Brownie Brittle after the first spin.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Run Mix-In, then serve immediately while the brittle pieces are still crunchy.

recipe.name: Money Mustard
recipe.description: High-Protein Chick-fil-A Style Sauce (with a Kick)
recipeIngredient: 30g Taste Flavor Co Cherry Smoked BBQ sauce
15g Fairlife Fat Free milk (~1 tbsp, for smoothing)
5g Taste Flavor Co Hot Honey Sriracha

recipeInstructions.name: Combine
recipeInstructions.text: Add everything to a bowl.

recipeInstructions.name: Whisk Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Whisk aggressively until fully combined. Texture should be creamy + pourable, not thick paste. If too thick, add 1-2 tsp more milk.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest
recipeInstructions.text: Let sit 10-15 minutes. Don't skip — this mellows the mustard, blends sweet + acid, and creates the Chick-fil-A balance.

recipe.name: Nilla Bean Float Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 5, Flavor 2 — cola-float-inspired protein Creami with vanilla, black cocoa, 1/4 cup Diet Coke in the base, and salted-caramel CocoRolls through Respin + on top. 340 cal / 43g protein whole pint. Slightly icier than a standard base — honest review.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1/4 cup Diet Coke (any diet cola — extra volume + slightly icier texture)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt + 1/2 tsp vanilla + 1 tbsp black cocoa + 1/4 cup Diet Coke. Immersion blender until completely smooth. Zero lumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Black Cocoa
recipeInstructions.text: Black cocoa (1 tbsp) supplies the float-adjacent dark identity. Regular cocoa reads brown-brown; black cocoa reads cola-black — the color and flavor cue are both from this ingredient.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Diet Cola
recipeInstructions.text: 1/4 cup diet cola stirred into the base pre-freeze. Volume goes up ~25% vs a standard base — the trade is a slightly icier texture. Any diet cola works; Diet Coke is what the creator filmed.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint, keeping the mixture below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes. Process on Regular Ice Cream. Powdery after the first spin is expected — the Respin fixes it.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in
recipeInstructions.text: Make a narrow center well. Drop in 1/2 serving of salted-caramel CocoRolls. Run RESPIN without adding liquid — the cola is already in the base.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop into a bowl. Volume will be noticeably taller than a standard pint — the cola quarter-cup shows up here.

recipeInstructions.name: Top + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Finish with another 1/4 serving of CocoRolls — added AFTER all machine processing so they stay crunchy. Eat immediately.

recipe.name: No-Judge Chimichurri
recipe.description: 60-second chimichurri. No chopping herbs. Steak-ready.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix
recipeInstructions.text: Combine olive oil, Spiceology chimichurri seasoning, red wine vinegar, and chili flakes in a small bowl.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest
recipeInstructions.text: Let sit 5-10 minutes. Don't skip — the vinegar blooms the dried herbs and the flavor develops.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Spoon over steak, chicken, or any grilled protein. 1 tbsp per serving.

recipe.name: High-Protein One-Pan Breakfast Skillet
recipe.description: 510 cal. 45g protein. 10 minutes. One pan. Eggs + Gilbert's Caprese + Lao Gan Ma.
recipeIngredient: 2 Gilbert's Craft Sausages Caprese Chicken Sausage links (basil + mozzarella + sun-dried tomato variant)
1 tsp Lao Gan Ma Fried Chili in Oil (NOT a tablespoon — 1 tsp is the macro lever)
Optional: black pepper or extra chili flakes

recipeInstructions.name: Spray The Pan
recipeInstructions.text: Nonstick skillet over medium heat. Hit with cooking spray.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sausage
recipeInstructions.text: 2 Gilbert's Caprese chicken sausage links into the pan. Cook 3-4 min, turning to brown all sides + warm through. The chicken sausage is pre-cooked — you're crisping the exterior, not cooking through raw meat.

recipeInstructions.name: Crack in The Eggs
recipeInstructions.text: 3 large eggs cracked directly into the skillet around the sausage links. Keep medium heat — too hot and the whites burn before the yolks set.

recipeInstructions.name: Season
recipeInstructions.text: Pinch of kosher salt over the eggs. Black pepper if using.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Chili Crisp
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma Fried Chili in Oil spooned over the eggs (focus on the crispy bits, light on the oil — the oil adds ~80 cal per tablespoon and you only want ~25 cal worth).

recipeInstructions.name: Cover + Set
recipeInstructions.text: Lid on. 2-4 min until whites are fully set and yolks are still jammy (or longer if you want them firm). Don't peek every 30 sec — open once at the 2-min mark.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve Hot
recipeInstructions.text: Slide everything onto a plate or eat straight from the skillet. The macro headline is 510 cal / 45g protein assuming 2 Gilbert's links + 3 eggs + 1 tsp Lao Gan Ma — any deviation shifts the math.

recipe.name: Orchard Cheddar Stackers Snack Box
recipe.description: Apple, cheese, sausage, and crackers in four kid-friendly compartments. About 270 calories and 13g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 2 servings Better Cheddars crackers — about 9 crackers per box
2 fully cooked Teton Waters Ranch beef Polish sausage links — ½ link per box
2 medium Honeycrisp apples — ½ apple per box
4 Frigo Cheese Heads Light mozzarella sticks — 1 stick per box

recipeInstructions.name: Heat The Sausage
recipeInstructions.text: Heat the fully cooked sausage according to the package directions. Let cool, then slice both links into kid-friendly coins.

recipeInstructions.name: Portion The Crackers
recipeInstructions.text: Put about 9 Better Cheddars in one compartment of each of four boxes. Pack separately if storing overnight so they stay crisp.

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Apple
recipeInstructions.text: Slice two Honeycrisp apples into age-appropriate pieces. Divide among the four boxes.

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Cut four light mozzarella sticks into coins; add one stick to each box.

recipeInstructions.name: Seal And Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Divide the cooled sausage among the boxes, seal, and refrigerate promptly. Pack with an ice pack when taking a box out.

recipe.name: Parmesan Corn Chex Snap Peas
recipe.description: Two-crunch side. 2 tbsp aged Parm + 4 tbsp crushed Corn Chex = the side that disappears off any plate.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups fresh sugar snap peas, trimmed (~12 oz)
2 tbsp Kirkland Parmigiano Reggiano Stravecchio, food-processed from a wedge to coarse grated
4 tbsp Corn Chex (General Mills), pulsed in food processor to coarse crumbs
Optional adult finish: cracked black pepper + lemon wedge at the table

recipeInstructions.text: PREHEAT OVEN 425°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

recipeInstructions.name: Process The Parm
recipeInstructions.text: Cube ~2 oz of Kirkland Stravecchio. Pulse in a food processor until coarse grated (NOT fine — you want visible flecks). Set aside.

recipeInstructions.name: Pulse The Chex
recipeInstructions.text: 4 tbsp Corn Chex into the same processor. Pulse 4-5 times until coarse crumbs — about the texture of panko, NOT powder. Visible flake bits are the goal.

recipeInstructions.name: Toss in a Bowl
recipeInstructions.text: Snap peas + olive oil spray (2-3 sec) + 2 tbsp processed Parm + 4 tbsp crushed Chex + pinch salt + pepper. Toss until each pea is coated. Toss in the bowl FIRST, then spread on the pan — even adherence beats sprinkling on the sheet.

recipeInstructions.name: Spread on Parchment
recipeInstructions.text: Single layer. Crumbs that fall onto the parchment will crisp into clusters — bonus crunch.

recipeInstructions.name: Bake 18-22 Min
recipeInstructions.text: 425°F. Pull when the snap pea edges are deep golden + the crust is crispy. Some pods will char slightly — that's the texture target.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve Immediately
recipeInstructions.text: Best straight from the oven. They soften on standing.

recipe.name: Peanut Butter Bar Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 6, Flavor 3 (Ep. 18) — PB2 in the base, half a zero-sugar oatmeal cookie through Respin, and a two-ingredient maple-cocoa hot fudge that may be the real winner. 330 cal / 47g protein whole pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1 tbsp PB2 powdered peanut butter (the only flavor addition)
1 tbsp sugar-free maple syrup (Maple Grove Farms filmed)
1 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa powder (sift, don't dump)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt + 1 tbsp PB2. Immersion blender until completely smooth. PB2 is the ONLY flavor addition — no vanilla, no emulsion.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Until Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Ensure the PB2 fully dissolves. Any clumps at this stage stay clumped through the freeze.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes. Process on Regular Ice Cream.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in Cookie
recipeInstructions.text: Break half a zero-sugar oatmeal cookie into rough chunks. Make a narrow center well, drop the chunks in, run RESPIN without adding liquid.

recipeInstructions.name: Warm Syrup
recipeInstructions.text: In a microwave-safe ramekin, warm 1 tbsp sugar-free maple syrup 10-15 seconds. Don't overheat — it thickens too fast as it cools if you do.

recipeInstructions.name: Sift Cocoa
recipeInstructions.text: Sift 1 tbsp Dutch cocoa into the warm syrup. Sifting is not optional — unsifted = gritty; sifted = silky.

recipeInstructions.name: Whisk Fudge
recipeInstructions.text: Whisk until no dry cocoa remains and the sauce reads silky and glossy. Aim for the consistency of warm chocolate syrup — it thickens as it cools.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the Respun Creami into a bowl.

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle the full hot-fudge batch over the scoop. Eat immediately — the fudge sets as it cools onto the frozen scoop.

recipe.name: Peanut Butter Cup Iced Proffee
recipe.description: Proffee Episode 4 — Ep 1's concentrate-first technique dressed up as a peanut butter cup. Chocolate-swirled cup + powdered peanut butter in the concentrate + Reese's Thin garnish. 160 cal / 23g protein per glass, 5-minute build.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp sugar-free chocolate syrup (drizzled around the inside of a tall serving cup)
1 tbsp instant coffee (creator's strong-coffee dose; use 1/2 tbsp for a milder drink)
1/2 serving unflavored whey isolate (~14g protein — adjust by brand)
2-3 tbsp hot water (hot but NOT boiling — start with 2 tbsp, add the third only if needed)
1/2 piece Reese's Thin, chopped or crumbled

recipeInstructions.name: Line The Cup
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle 1 tbsp sugar-free chocolate syrup around the INSIDE of a tall serving cup. Not on the bottom — spiral it around the interior wall so each sip picks up more chocolate as the drink drains.

BUILD CONCENTRATE (into the chocolate-lined cup): 1 tbsp instant coffee + 1/2 serving unflavored whey isolate + 1/2 tbsp powdered peanut butter + 2 tsp monk fruit sweetener. Powdered peanut butter (not spread) is the macro pick — peanut flavor without a fat load.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Hot Water + Froth
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp hot (not boiling) water. Submerge the frother BEFORE turning it on. Froth until completely smooth. Add the third tbsp only if the concentrate needs help moving.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Ice + Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Fill the cup with ice, then pour in 1/2 cup Fairlife fat-free ultra-filtered milk. Stir gently if you want the chocolate swirl incorporated immediately; leave it undisturbed if you want the sip-by-sip chocolate pull.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Top with 1 tbsp sugar-free whipped cream and half a chopped or crumbled Reese's Thin. Serve immediately — whipped cream softens against the cold in 1-2 minutes.

recipe.name: Pineapple Ham CocoRolls Snack Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 14 — sweet-and-savory kid snack box: fresh pineapple, Hempler's Black Forest uncured ham, Great Value light mozzarella, and Sun Tropics Salted Caramel CocoRolls. ~230 cal / 17g protein per box. 4 boxes = 2 kids across 2 days.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups fresh pineapple chunks — 1/2 cup per box
8 oz Hempler's Black Forest uncured ham — 2 oz per box
4 Great Value light mozzarella string cheese sticks — 1 stick per box, cut into bite-size pieces
2 servings Sun Tropics Salted Caramel CocoRolls — 1/2 serving per box

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Pineapple
recipeInstructions.text: Place roughly 1/2 cup fresh pineapple chunks in one compartment of each of the 4 boxes. Cut age-appropriate — smaller for toddlers.

recipeInstructions.name: Portion The Ham
recipeInstructions.text: Fold or cut 2 oz of Hempler's Black Forest uncured ham into one compartment of each box. This is the main protein anchor — ~73 cal / 10g protein per 2 oz.

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Mozzarella
recipeInstructions.text: Cut 1 Great Value light mozzarella string cheese into bite-size pieces for each box. ~50 cal / 6g protein per stick — the second protein tier.

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Cocorolls
recipeInstructions.text: Finish each box with half a serving of Sun Tropics Salted Caramel CocoRolls. Pack whole for maximum crunch. CocoRolls contain egg and coconut — recheck the label if managing an allergy.

recipeInstructions.name: Seal + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lids on and refrigerate. Serve within 2 days. Transport with an ice pack. For maximum crunch, pack the CocoRolls separately and add them at serving time.

recipe.name: Pineapple Whip Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 2, Flavor 1 — pineapple-fruit-cup + yellow-color stirred into the standard base BEFORE freezing (no machine mix-in), Regular Ice Cream cycle, graham crumble on top. ~340 cal / 42g protein whole pint vs the 760-cal Crumbl Pineapple Whip Cookie on the current Gawinder listing.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1 single-serve pineapple tidbits fruit cup in 100% juice (~60 cal)
A few drops yellow food coloring (optional, for visual cue)
40 cal graham crackers, crushed (roughly 1/2 sheet Honey Maid or equivalent)

recipeInstructions.name: Pour Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk to a Creami pint (or blending vessel).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sweetener
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener. Same series-standard sweetener as the Week 1 flavors.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Whey Isolate
recipeInstructions.text: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate. Aim for ~28g protein — brands vary, so read the scoop.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Guar Gum
recipeInstructions.text: 1/8 tsp guar gum, LEVEL measure. Heaped = gummy texture. This is the single measurement in the base you actually have to get right.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Salt
recipeInstructions.text: 1 pinch salt. Blend the whole base — immersion blender until completely smooth. Zero lumps. Zero visible whey.

recipeInstructions.name: Stir in Pineapple
recipeInstructions.text: Add the entire single-serve pineapple tidbits fruit cup (juice + fruit). STIR IT IN — do NOT blend. Preserve the pineapple tidbits so they carry through the finished pint. This is the technique twist that makes this flavor.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Yellow Color
recipeInstructions.text: A few drops of yellow food coloring. Optional but recommended — the visual cue is what makes the finished pint read as Pineapple Whip on first look. Stir to distribute.

recipeInstructions.name: Gently Blend / Stir
recipeInstructions.text: Stir the pineapple + color through the base until evenly distributed. Do not over-work — the goal is tidbits suspended in colored base, not a smooth pineapple puree.

recipeInstructions.name: Pint Ready to Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint (if you didn't build in the pint already), staying below the max-fill line. Cap and set upright on a level freezer shelf.

FREEZE (24 HR) + REST 5 MIN + PROCESS REGULAR ICE CREAM: Full 24 hours upright and level. Rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes — NO hot-water bath. Process on Regular Ice Cream, NOT Lite. If the first spin comes out powdery, run ONE Respin. Otherwise scoop immediately.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the finished pint into a bowl. Pineapple tidbits should be visible pulled through the pale-yellow Creami.

recipeInstructions.name: Graham Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Crush ~40 cal of graham crackers over the scoops (roughly 1/2 sheet). Serve immediately — graham softens fast on ice cream.

recipe.name: Pink Berry Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 5, Flavor 1 — buttery strawberry protein Creami pint inspired by Crumbl's Pink Berry Cookie. Brown-butter emulsion carries the cookie note; freeze-dried strawberries stay crunchy on top. 315 cal / 43g protein whole pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1/4 tsp brown-butter emulsion (LorAnn Brown Butter Bakery Emulsion)
1/2 serving vanilla wafers (HighKey filmed — recalculate macros if substituting)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt + 1/4 tsp strawberry emulsion + 1/4 tsp brown-butter emulsion. Immersion blender until completely smooth. Zero lumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint, keeping the mixture below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes. Process on Regular Ice Cream (not Lite). Powdery after the first spin is expected — the Respin fixes it.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in
recipeInstructions.text: Make a narrow center well. Drop in half a serving of vanilla wafers. Run RESPIN without adding liquid.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop into a bowl. The Respin should give a smooth, evenly-mixed pink base with visible wafer pockets.

recipeInstructions.name: Top + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Finish with 4g freeze-dried strawberries — added AFTER all machine processing so they stay crunchy. Eat immediately.

recipe.name: Pistachio Kataifi Protein Creami
recipe.description: Ninja Creami ice cream that hits ~35g protein. Engineered, not guessed.
recipeIngredient: Opportuniteas Whey Isolate (~28g protein total — adjust scoops by brand)
1/8 tsp Bob's Red Mill Guar Gum

recipeInstructions.name: Blend
recipeInstructions.text: Combine milk, protein powder, cocoa, monk fruit, guar gum, and salt. Use immersion blender until completely smooth.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into Ninja Creami pint container. Freeze flat for 12-16 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Pre-spin
recipeInstructions.text: Run hot water over the outside of the container for 30 seconds.

recipeInstructions.name: Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Select Regular Ice Cream. Re-spin once if needed — no extra milk.

recipeInstructions.name: Assemble
recipeInstructions.text: Swirl in pistachio cream. Top with toasted kataifi. Eat immediately.

recipe.name: Pita Hummus Snack Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 13 — smoky chipotle chicken, Colby Jack, everything pita crackers, cucumber, and half a single-serve hummus cup on the side. ~300 cal / 18g protein per box. 4 boxes = 2 kids across 2 days.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz grilled chipotle seasoned chicken (fully cooked) — 2 oz per box
4 Colby Jack snack cheese pieces — 1 piece per box
4 labeled servings everything pita crackers — 1 serving per box
Cucumber, as needed — peel and cut age-appropriate to fill one compartment per box
2 single-serve classic hummus cups (2 oz each) — split each cup across 2 boxes; 1 oz hummus per box

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Line up 4 divided snack boxes. Buluker pastel 4-compartment boxes shown — the same set featured on Favorites → Snack Box Essentials.

recipeInstructions.name: Chipotle Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: Portion 2 oz of fully cooked chipotle chicken into each box. This is the protein anchor — Costco grilled chipotle chicken was filmed at 100 cal / 16g protein per 3 oz serving.

recipeInstructions.name: Colby Jack
recipeInstructions.text: Place 1 wrapped Colby Jack snack cheese in one compartment of each box. Tillamook Colby Jack was filmed — mild flavor pairs with the smoky chicken.

recipeInstructions.name: Everything Pita Crackers
recipeInstructions.text: 1 labeled serving in one compartment. Town House Pita Everything was filmed. Pack whole for maximum crunch and let the kid break at snack time.

recipeInstructions.name: Cucumber
recipeInstructions.text: Peel if desired and cut into age-appropriate pieces. Fill the remaining compartment. Cucumber is the second-crunch tier and the freshener.

recipeInstructions.name: Hummus on The Side — 1 oz Per Box
recipeInstructions.text: Split each 2-oz single-serve hummus cup between 2 boxes = 1 oz per box in a small leakproof side cup. 365 by Whole Foods Original Hummus 2 oz singles were filmed. THE FILMED SERVING SHOWS A FULL 2-OZ CUP PER BOX — that was too much. Half a cup is plenty and holds the ~300-cal / 18g-protein target.

recipeInstructions.name: Seal + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lids on and refrigerate. Serve within 2 days. Transport with an ice pack. Keep the hummus side cup sealed separately for leak-proof travel.

recipe.name: Protein Blue Cheese Crema
recipe.description: Tastes like real blue cheese sauce. Quietly protein-forward.
recipeIngredient: 113g 365 Blue Cheese Crumbles (4 oz container, full)
1 tsp lemon juice (the acid that sharpens it — don't skip)
1 tsp Dan-O's SPG Tri-O (Salt-Pepper-Garlic — does the work of fresh garlic without the harsh bite)
