1 tbsp fresh chives, finely chopped (FOLDED IN AFTER blending — never blend, or the sauce turns green)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Cottage cheese + Fairlife + lemon juice + SPG Tri-O in a blender or immersion-blender cup. Blend 60 sec on high until completely smooth — zero curd visible. This is the texture move.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Blue Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Add about 80% of the blue cheese crumbles. Pulse 5-6 times — you want the sauce blue-cheese-flavored but with visible chunks. NOT smooth all the way through.

recipeInstructions.name: Fold in Chunks + Chives
recipeInstructions.text: Stir the remaining 20% of crumbles + all the chopped chives in by hand. Chives go in LAST so they don't blend and turn the sauce green.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest
recipeInstructions.text: Fridge, 10-15 minutes. Lemon mellows, blue cheese funk deepens, texture tightens. Non-negotiable.

recipeInstructions.name: Taste
recipeInstructions.text: Too sharp? Add 1 tbsp more cottage cheese. Too thick? 1 tsp more milk. Not funky enough? Crumble in a few more chunks of blue cheese.

recipe.name: Protein Cereal Hack
recipe.description: Keep your cereal. Upgrade your milk.
recipeIngredient: 28g cereal (1 measured serving — S'mores, Cinnamon Toast Crunch, whatever you like)
1/2 cup Fairlife Fat Free Ultra-Filtered Milk
1/2 serving Opportuniteas Grass-Fed Whey Protein Isolate (unflavored)

recipeInstructions.name: Mix Protein Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1/2 scoop unflavored whey isolate to 1/2 cup Fairlife. Shake or whisk until fully smooth. No clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour
recipeInstructions.text: Pour protein milk over 28g measured cereal.

recipeInstructions.name: Eat
recipeInstructions.text: That's it. No cooking, no prep.

recipe.name: Protein Cheesecake Frosting
recipe.description: Cheesecake-style frosting that lives in a jar. 30g serving = 60 cal / 6g protein. 15 servings per batch, 5-min blend, no cook.
recipeIngredient: 215g Philadelphia 1/3 Less Fat Cream Cheese (1 brick — Neufchâtel)
15g Jell-O Sugar-Free Cheesecake Instant Pudding Mix (about half a 1 oz box)
15g Whole Earth Monk Fruit Erythritol Blend
62g PEScience Select Gourmet Vanilla Protein Powder (2 scoops)

recipeInstructions.name: Add Skyr
recipeInstructions.text: 225g Siggi's 0% Plain Skyr into a blender cup or small food processor.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Cream Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: 215g Philadelphia 1/3 Less Fat Cream Cheese on top of the skyr. Best if the cream cheese is at room temperature — soft cream cheese blends without leaving pockets.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Pudding + Sweetener
recipeInstructions.text: 15g Jell-O Sugar-Free Cheesecake Instant Pudding Mix (about half a 1 oz box) + 15g Whole Earth Monk Fruit Erythritol Blend. Drop both in dry — they hydrate during the blend.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Vanilla Protein
recipeInstructions.text: 62g PEScience Select Gourmet Vanilla Protein Powder (2 scoops). Drop on top last so it doesn't poof out when the blender starts.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: 30-60 sec on high until thick, glossy, and pourable. Stop + scrape down the sides at 30 sec if needed — protein powder can stick to the walls. Should look like thick cake frosting that just barely flows.

recipeInstructions.name: Transfer to Jar
recipeInstructions.text: Spoon into a clean glass jar (16 oz mason jar fits the batch perfectly with a bit of headroom). Scraping with a spatula = your batch math; what stays in the blender = the 80g you lose to transfer.

recipeInstructions.name: Refrigerate
recipeInstructions.text: Seal the jar. Refrigerate. The texture sets slightly firmer overnight — stir before serving on day 2+. Eat within 5 days.

recipe.name: Protein Corn Flakes
recipe.description: The 'this shouldn't work but somehow does' high-protein cereal. Hot Nurri + dry flakes = warm vanilla cereal milk that hits 34g protein.
recipeIngredient: 2 oz Kellogg's Corn Flakes (about 1.5 cups — the Family Size box is the move)
1 can Nurri Vanilla Ultra-Filtered Milk Shake (11 fl oz, 30g protein)

recipeInstructions.text: WARM THE NURRI (the hot version — your default): Pour the entire Nurri can into a microwave-safe bowl or mug. Microwave 2 minutes. It comes out hot but not boiling — almost like steamed milk.

recipeInstructions.name: Portion The Flakes
recipeInstructions.text: 2 oz of Kellogg's Corn Flakes into a separate bowl. Eyeball it at about 1.5 cups — measuring matters less here than for most cereals.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Eat Immediately
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the hot Nurri over the flakes. Eat in the next 90 seconds — you want the flakes partially crisp, not fully soggy. The window matters.

recipeInstructions.name: Alternate (cold Version)
recipeInstructions.text: Skip the microwave. Pour Nurri straight from the can over the flakes. Standard cereal experience, just with thick protein milk instead of thin almond milk that waters out the flavor.

recipe.name: Protein Tiramisu
recipe.description: Sunday-night build. 4 servings, overnight chill, 24g protein per ramekin.
recipeIngredient: 150g Fage Total 0% Greek Yogurt (1 small container)
84g Philadelphia Neufchâtel Cheese (3 portions of an 8 oz block)
2 scoops PEScience Select Protein, Vanilla (62g total)
3 tbsp Whole Earth Allulose + Monk Fruit sweetener blend (36g)
28 HighKey Vanilla Wafers (7 per ramekin × 4 ramekins, ~70g total)
About 1/2 cup black coffee (brewed strong, room temp) — for dipping the wafers only
1/2 tbsp Ghirardelli unsweetened cocoa powder (for the snowfall on top)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Cottage Cheese Alone
recipeInstructions.text: This is the most important step. Add the full 150g Daisy 2% to a blender or food processor. Blend until completely smooth — no visible curds. If you skip this and blend everything together, surviving curds wreck the mousse texture and you'll taste them all week. Non-negotiable.

recipeInstructions.name: Add The Rest of The Cream
recipeInstructions.text: Once cottage cheese is silky, add the Fage 0%, Neufchâtel (cut into chunks so it blends), 2 scoops PEScience Vanilla, and 3 tbsp Whole Earth sweetener. No coffee goes in the cream — all the coffee is in the wafer dip. Blend until thick, smooth, mousse-like — should hold a soft peak, not pour. If too thick, add a splash of milk or water.

recipeInstructions.name: Brew The Dip Coffee
recipeInstructions.text: Brew about 1/2 cup strong black coffee and cool it to room temp. Pour into a shallow bowl wide enough to lay a wafer flat. This is the only coffee in the recipe.

recipeInstructions.name: Dip, Don't Soak
recipeInstructions.text: One wafer at a time — quick in, quick out. Roughly one second per side. The wafer should still feel structural when you place it. Soaked wafers turn into wet sludge by morning. This is where most home tiramisus die.

recipeInstructions.name: Layer
recipeInstructions.text: In each of 4 ramekins or 6 oz meal-prep containers — 3-4 dipped wafers on the bottom (snap if needed to fit), generous spoonful of cream (~1/4 of cream total ÷ 2 layers = ~1/8 per layer), 3-4 more dipped wafers, another generous spoonful of cream on top (7 wafers per ramekin × 4 ramekins = 28 wafers total). Smooth flat. Repeat for all 4 containers.

CHILL OVERNIGHT — NOT 4 HOURS, OVERNIGHT: This is the second non-negotiable step. The protein powder needs to hydrate, the wafers need to soften from the coffee dip, and the flavors need to meld. Day 2 tastes dramatically better than fresh — the coffee bitterness smooths out and the cream sets like real tiramisu cream.

recipeInstructions.name: Cocoa Dust Right Before Eating
recipeInstructions.text: Don't dust ahead of time — cocoa absorbs moisture and goes patchy. Divide the listed 1/2 tbsp Ghirardelli cocoa among the four containers, dusting each only when you eat it. Use a fine mesh strainer for an even snowfall. The cocoa carries the tiramisu perception harder than anything else in the recipe.

recipe.name: Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Protein Creami
recipe.description: Real pumpkin, thick protein ice cream and milk-chocolate chips. About 280 calories and 28g protein for the whole finished pint.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 serving Opportuniteas unflavored whey · 60 cal / 14g protein
3 pumps Syruvia sugar-free Pumpkin Spice syrup
14g Lily’s milk-chocolate-style chips · into the pint

recipeInstructions.name: Blend
recipeInstructions.text: Combine milk, half-serving whey, three syrup pumps, pumpkin puree, guar gum and salt. Blend smooth in the pint, below its fill line.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Freeze upright and level for 24 hours. Rest on the counter for five minutes, following the creator’s usual process and your machine’s instructions.

recipeInstructions.name: Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Process on Regular Ice Cream. This batch was thick and needed an extra spin. Pumpkin puree may have contributed, but that was not isolated or tested.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Chips + Respin
recipeInstructions.text: Add 14g Lily’s milk-chocolate-style chips after the initial spin and process using the creator’s usual Respin method. Respin, rather than Mix-In, is the filmed method. Follow the manual for your exact machine.

recipeInstructions.name: Top + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop into a bowl. Add one more pump of the same pumpkin-spice syrup and 7g of the same chocolate chips.

recipe.name: Rainbow Shake Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 6, Flavor 2 (Ep. 17) — brown-butter vanilla protein Creami with mini M&M's through Respin + a deliberately overloaded garnish on top. 360 cal / 42g protein whole pint. Honest verdict: fine but basic, and one full ounce of candy is finally candy overload.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt + 1/4 tsp brown-butter emulsion + 1/2 tsp vanilla extract. Immersion blender until completely smooth.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Vanilla
recipeInstructions.text: Vanilla goes in with the emulsion — both pre-freeze. This is the entire flavor identity of the base.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes. Process on Regular Ice Cream.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in Mini M&m's
recipeInstructions.text: Make a narrow center well. Drop in 0.5 oz (14g) mini M&M's. Run RESPIN without adding liquid — this distributes candy-shell crunch through the pint.

recipeInstructions.name: Respin Result
recipeInstructions.text: Post-Respin should read as a creamy vanilla base flecked with M&M pieces. If it's still powdery, add nothing and Respin one more time.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop into a bowl. The second 0.5 oz of mini M&M's stays out of the machine — it's a garnish, not a mix-in.

recipeInstructions.name: Garnish
recipeInstructions.text: Scatter the second 0.5 oz (14g) of mini M&M's across the scoop. Eat immediately — candy crunch is best in the first 2-3 minutes.

recipe.name: Red Velvet Cookie Thins Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 3, Flavor 3 — Week 3 finale. Rose-mauve red velvet protein Creami with fudgy protein-brownie pockets Respun through the pint and a POST-SCOOP white-chocolate drizzle. ~370 cal / 48g protein whole pint — original Creami adaptation inspired by the Crumbl Red Velvet Cookie Thins (Set of 2).
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1/2 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa powder (HALF the Mallow/Dubai charge)
1 tsp red velvet emulsion (LorAnn or similar — full dose, not corrected)
1/3 of a red velvet protein brownie, chopped (~75 cal — verify current label)
1 tbsp Fairlife fat-free ultra-filtered milk (thinner than 2% — helps the drizzle pour)

recipeInstructions.name: Pour Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk to a Creami pint (or blending vessel).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sweetener
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Whey Isolate
recipeInstructions.text: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Guar Gum
recipeInstructions.text: 1/8 tsp guar gum, LEVEL measure. Heaped = gummy.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Salt
recipeInstructions.text: 1 pinch salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Dutch Cocoa
recipeInstructions.text: 1/2 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa powder. HALF the Mallow/Dubai charge (both used 1 tbsp) — the reduced cocoa lets the red velvet emulsion + white-chocolate drizzle carry the identity, not the cocoa. Straight cocoa charge would make it read as 'plain chocolate ice cream with red dye', which misses the red velvet cream-cheese identity.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Red Velvet Emulsion
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tsp red velvet emulsion. Full dose (not publish-corrected like W3F2 Dubai's 1/2 tsp pistachio emulsion). Red velvet emulsion is the identity carrier across the whole pint since there's no strong topping identity like Dubai's kataifi crunch — the emulsion has to do more work in the base here. LorAnn is the most common food-grade red velvet emulsion; also colors the base a rose-mauve tone from the natural red pigment.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Immersion blender until completely smooth. Base should be a uniform rose-mauve tone — the Dutch cocoa + red velvet emulsion together read as a warm pink-brown, NOT deep chocolate and NOT bright red. Zero lumps, zero visible whey.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer to a Creami pint if you didn't build in the pint. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours. Do not exceed the max-fill line.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest 5 Min + First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the frozen pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes — NO hot-water bath. Process on Regular Ice Cream, NOT Lite. The first spin may look powdery; expected because the Respin (with brownie pieces) finishes the texture.

recipeInstructions.name: Chop Brownie
recipeInstructions.text: Chop 1/3 of a red velvet protein brownie into small pieces (~1/4 inch cubes). ~75 cal of brownie is the target — verify the current package weight and adjust the portion if the bar size has changed. Same technique family as W3F1 Mallow (which used the Cookie Monster Prime Bites brownie); this ep uses a RED VELVET protein brownie for flavor continuity with the base emulsion.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Brownie + Respin
recipeInstructions.text: Make a well in the center of the first-spin pint and press the brownie pieces down into the well (better distribution than piling on top). Run one Respin cycle. Respin distributes the brownie pieces AND finishes the powdery texture from the first spin. Same technique family as W3F1 Mallow — different brownie flavor.

recipeInstructions.name: Respin Result
recipeInstructions.text: The finished Respin should show visible red velvet brownie pieces distributed through the pint with a smooth, non-powdery Creami texture. If the texture still reads powdery, run a second Respin.

recipeInstructions.name: Melt White Chocolate + ff Milk
recipeInstructions.text: In a small microwave-safe bowl, combine 1 tbsp white chocolate chips + 1 tbsp Fairlife FAT-FREE ultra-filtered milk (NOT 2% — fat-free thins the drizzle to a pourable consistency; 2% would set thicker). Microwave in 10-15 second bursts, stirring between each, until fully smooth. Do not overheat — white chocolate seizes fast if boiled. Series-first: no prior CCC ep used a melted-white-chocolate drizzle finish.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the finished pint into a bowl. Rose-mauve Creami with visible red velvet brownie pockets pulled through the scoops.

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the warm white-chocolate mixture over the scoops in a slow ribbon. The drizzle is a POST-SCOOP GARNISH — not a machine mix-in. Adding white chocolate to the pint before Respin would set into hard chunks that shatter unpleasantly against cold Creami. Keeping it as a post-scoop drizzle preserves the smooth ribbon and the cream-frosting identity moment. Serve immediately — the drizzle starts to firm as it cools against the cold pint.

recipe.name: Salmon Cream Cheese Bagel
recipe.description: 5-minute smoked salmon cream cheese bagel — 250 cal / 30g protein on a Sola high-protein bagel. No deli build, no toast.

recipeInstructions.name: Salmon
recipeInstructions.text: Add the smoked salmon to a cutting board.

recipeInstructions.name: Cream Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Drop 2 tbsp cream cheese on top of the salmon.

recipeInstructions.name: Chop
recipeInstructions.text: Chop the salmon and cream cheese together with a chef's knife into a chunky spread. Don't whip it smooth — salmon should stay visible in small pieces.

recipeInstructions.name: Open
recipeInstructions.text: Halve the Sola bagel.

recipeInstructions.name: Load
recipeInstructions.text: Spread the chunky salmon cream cheese onto both bagel halves.

recipeInstructions.name: Eat
recipeInstructions.text: Eat immediately — bagel toasts in the spread's residual fat if you want a quick pan-warm.

recipe.name: Salted Caramel Pretzel Iced Proffee
recipe.description: Proffee Episode 3 — Ep 1's concentrate technique with a Snyder's pretzel + Skinny Syrups salted caramel rim, LorAnn caramel emulsion in the concentrate, and Reddi-wip Zero Sugar on top. 140 cal / 21g protein per glass, 5-minute build.
recipeIngredient: 0.25 oz Snyder's of Hanover mini pretzels, crushed (total for rim + garnish)
To taste, Skinny Syrups Sugar-Free Salted Caramel (rim coating + finishing drizzle)
1/2 serving unflavored whey isolate (~14g protein — adjust by brand)
2-3 tbsp hot water (hot but NOT boiling — start with 2 tbsp, add the third only if needed)
1 tbsp Reddi-wip Zero Sugar whipped topping
Skinny Syrups Sugar-Free Salted Caramel drizzle to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Crush + Divide Pretzels
recipeInstructions.text: 0.25 oz Snyder's mini pretzels crushed into small pieces. Reserve part for the finish; the rest goes on the rim.

recipeInstructions.name: Rim The Empty Glass
recipeInstructions.text: Pour a shallow layer of Skinny Syrups salted caramel into a small bowl. Dip the rim of the tall serving glass in the caramel, then press it into the crushed pretzels. Rim the glass empty so caramel doesn't run down a full drink.
BUILD CONCENTRATE (into the rimmed glass, keep rim undisturbed): 1/2 tbsp instant coffee + 1/2 serving unflavored whey isolate + 2 tsp monk fruit + 1/2 tsp LorAnn caramel emulsion.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Hot Water + Blend
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp hot (not boiling) water. Submerge the immersion-blender head BEFORE turning it on. Blend smooth. Add the third tbsp only if the concentrate needs help moving.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Ice + Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Ice to the level you want, then 1/2 cup Fairlife fat-free ultra-filtered milk over the ice. Stir gently — don't disturb the pretzel rim.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tbsp Reddi-wip Zero Sugar on top, drizzle with Skinny Syrups salted caramel, garnish with the reserved pretzel pieces. Stir and serve immediately.

recipe.name: Shirley Temple Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 5, Flavor 3 (WEEK 5 FINALE / Ep. 15) — Shirley-Temple-inspired protein Creami: base carries lime gelatin + vanilla + brown-butter emulsion pre-freeze, mix-in is HighKey vanilla wafers via Respin, finished with a restrained 1/3 oz regular grenadine drizzle + one maraschino cherry. 340 cal / 43g protein whole pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1/3 oz regular grenadine syrup (light drizzle only)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt + lime gelatin + vanilla + brown-butter emulsion. Immersion blender until completely smooth. Zero lumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Lime Gelatin Note
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tsp of Jell-O lime gelatin goes into the base pre-freeze. Used as a texture-only additive (echoing W2F3 Key Lime, but the lime here is a background note, not the flavor identity). Noticeably improved the finished texture — may be tested in the standard series base.

recipeInstructions.name: Brown-butter + Vanilla
recipeInstructions.text: 1/4 tsp brown-butter emulsion + 1/2 tsp vanilla supply the buttery cookie note. Emulsion holds through freezing better than butter itself.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes. Process on Regular Ice Cream. Powdery after the first spin is expected — the Respin fixes it.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in Wafers
recipeInstructions.text: Make a narrow center well. Drop in 0.5 oz (14g) of HighKey vanilla wafers. Run RESPIN without adding liquid.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop + Grenadine
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop into a bowl. Drizzle 1/3 oz of regular grenadine LIGHTLY over the top — sugar-containing syrup, intentionally restrained, and never added to the frozen base.

recipeInstructions.name: Top + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Finish with one maraschino cherry. Eat immediately — the wafer crunch is best in the first 2-3 minutes.

recipe.name: 365-Calorie Smoky Chipotle Chicken Burritos
recipe.description: Quick Lunches Ep. 3 — two burritos: Kirkland chipotle chicken, Smoky Chipotle Crema, Mezete pickled red onions, on Mission Carb Balance tortillas. ~365 cal / 49g protein (est.) for both.
recipeIngredient: 2 Mission Carb Balance tortillas (~70 cal each)
6 oz Kirkland / Costco shortcut chipotle chicken (fully cooked)
1/2 serving Smoky Chipotle Crema (~1 1/2 tbsp; cross-link to /cookbook/smoky-chipotle-crema)
Mezete pickled red onions, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Reheat Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: Air-fry 6 oz Kirkland chipotle chicken about 10 minutes per the package guidance, until hot and 165 F. Appliance settings vary — no temperature invented; use your air fryer's default reheat preset.

recipeInstructions.name: Sauce Tortillas
recipeInstructions.text: Lay out both Mission Carb Balance tortillas. Divide the Smoky Chipotle Crema evenly between them, spreading in the center — leave the tortilla edges dry so they seal cleanly when rolled.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Crunch
recipeInstructions.text: Scatter Mezete pickled red onions to taste over the crema. The onions go under the chicken so they don't wilt from the hot chicken making contact directly.

recipeInstructions.name: Fill With Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: Divide the hot chipotle chicken evenly between both tortillas. Keep the fill line in the center third — over-fill and the tortilla will split at the roll.

recipeInstructions.name: Roll + Eat
recipeInstructions.text: Fold in the sides of each tortilla, roll tightly toward the far edge, and eat immediately while the chicken is hot and the tortilla is soft.

recipe.name: Smoky Chipotle Crema
recipe.description: Bold. Smoky. Proper heat. Built the way it should be.
recipeIngredient: 7 oz (198g) La Costeña Chipotle Peppers in Adobo (full can)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend
recipeInstructions.text: Add everything to blender — yogurt, full chipotle can + adobo, milk, mayo, lime juice, salt, garlic powder, cumin. Blend 30-45 seconds until fully smooth.

recipeInstructions.name: Taste
recipeInstructions.text: Too thick → add 1 tbsp milk. Too sharp → add 1 tbsp yogurt. Too flat → pinch more salt + lime.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest
recipeInstructions.text: Let sit 10-15 minutes before serving. Heat rounds out, texture tightens. Don't skip.

recipe.name: S'mores Brownie Cookie Protein Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 11 Flavor 3 — brown-butter protein Creami with a quarter Prime Bites brownie, Nilla Minis, and Lily's milk-chocolate chips through Mix-In, finished with marshmallow creme. About 395 calories and 45g protein for the complete pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 batch usual protein Creami base (240 cal / 40g protein)
1/2 tsp LorAnn Brown Butter Bakery Emulsion (blend into base before freezing; no vanilla)
1/4 Prime Bites Chocolate Glazed Donut protein brownie
10g Nilla Minis (optional — disappeared under the other mix-ins on film)
7g Lily's Milk Chocolate Style baking chips

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Blend 1/2 teaspoon LorAnn brown-butter bakery emulsion into your usual protein Creami base until completely smooth. No vanilla — the emulsion is the whole flavor.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint without exceeding the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level overnight.

recipeInstructions.name: First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Rest the pint 5 minutes, then process on Regular Ice Cream. If it stays powdery, run one no-liquid Respin before the mix-in.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1/4 Prime Bites brownie, 10g Nilla Minis, and 7g Lily's milk-chocolate chips, then run Mix-In.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop + Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the Creami into a bowl and finish with 1 tablespoon marshmallow creme. Eat immediately for the intended texture.

recipe.name: S'mores Iced Proffee
recipe.description: Proffee Episode 5 — Ep 1's concentrate-first technique with a thin marshmallow-creme + graham rim, two toasted marshmallows, and a sugar-free chocolate drizzle. 150 cal / 22g protein per glass, 5-minute build.
recipeIngredient: very thin smear marshmallow creme (rim coat only — a heavy layer overwhelms the drink and messes up the glass)
1/2 sheet graham cracker, crushed on a plate
1 tbsp instant coffee (creator's strong-coffee dose; use 1/2 tbsp for a milder drink)
1/2 serving unflavored whey isolate (~14g protein — adjust by brand)
2-3 tbsp hot water (hot but NOT boiling — start with 2 tbsp, add the third only if needed)
2 pieces Max Mallow marshmallows (or equivalent low-calorie marshmallows — macros vary by brand)
1/2 tbsp sugar-free chocolate syrup, for drizzling

recipeInstructions.name: Build The S'mores Rim
recipeInstructions.text: Spread a VERY THIN smear of marshmallow creme around the rim of a tall serving glass. Crush half a graham cracker sheet on a plate and press the coated rim into the crumbs. Rim coat only — a heavy layer overwhelms the coffee and makes the glass messy.

BUILD THE CONCENTRATE (into the rimmed glass): 1 tbsp instant coffee + 1/2 serving unflavored whey isolate + 2 tsp monk fruit sweetener. Blend the whey into the concentrate FIRST — this is the Proffee-series spine that prevents clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Hot Water + Froth
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp hot (not boiling) water. Submerge the frother head BEFORE turning it on for splatter control. Froth until the concentrate is completely smooth. Add the third tbsp only if it needs help moving.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Ice + Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Fill the glass with ice, then pour in 1/2 cup Fairlife fat-free ultra-filtered milk. Stir gently.

recipeInstructions.name: Toast The Marshmallows Safely
recipeInstructions.text: Place the two Max Mallow marshmallows on a heat-safe skewer or utensil and torch them AWAY from the glass and any plastic. Skewer method is the safest and cleanest — never torch marshmallows already sitting in the drink. Set the toasted marshmallows over the glass.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle 1/2 tbsp sugar-free chocolate syrup over the toasted marshmallows and serve immediately. Marshmallow rim softens against ambient humidity in ~5 minutes.

recipe.name: Snickerdoodle Cookie Creami
recipe.description: Vanilla-cinnamon protein Creami with Cinnamon Toast Crunch mixed through the pint. About 285 calories and 28g protein for the whole finished pint.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 serving Opportuniteas unflavored whey (60 calories, 14g protein per serving)
21g Cinnamon Toast Crunch, added after the first spin

recipeInstructions.name: Blend
recipeInstructions.text: Blend the milk, whey, sweetener, guar gum, salt, vanilla, and cinnamon until smooth.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into one Creami pint below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Rest on the counter for five minutes, then run Regular Ice Cream following your machine instructions. If powdery, use a no-liquid Respin before adding cereal.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in
recipeInstructions.text: Add 21g Cinnamon Toast Crunch and run Mix-In. If needed, Respin without added liquid only until the cereal is incorporated. No topping is added.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the complete pint; the measured cereal is mixed through it, with no topping.

recipe.name: Snickerdoodle Skillet Cookie Protein Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 11 Flavor 1 — vanilla-cinnamon protein Creami with Cinnamon Toast Crunch through Mix-In and a melted Lily's white chocolate drizzle plus more cereal on top. About 400 calories and 41g protein for the complete pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 batch usual protein Creami base (240 cal / 40g protein)
1 tsp vanilla extract (blend into base before freezing)
1 tsp ground cinnamon (blend into base before freezing)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Blend 1 teaspoon vanilla and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon into your usual protein Creami base until completely smooth.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint without exceeding the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level overnight.

recipeInstructions.name: First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Rest the pint 5 minutes, then process on Regular Ice Cream. If it stays powdery, run one no-liquid Respin before the mix-in.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in The Cereal
recipeInstructions.text: Add 10g Cinnamon Toast Crunch and run Mix-In.

recipeInstructions.name: Melt The White Chocolate
recipeInstructions.text: Melt 14g Lily's white chocolate chips until smooth and pourable.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop + Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the Creami into a bowl, drizzle the melted white chocolate, and top with the remaining 10g Cinnamon Toast Crunch. Eat immediately for the intended texture.

recipe.name: SNICKERS Peanut Butter Cookie Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 4, Flavor 1 — powdered-peanut-butter protein Creami pint, peanut-caramel protein bar Respin, sugar-free chocolate drizzle, and chopped bar on top. ~370 cal / 53g protein whole pint — highest-protein CCC ep so far.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1 tbsp powdered peanut butter (e.g., PB2, PBfit — any brand)
1/4 of a peanut-caramel protein bar, chopped small (Barebells Salty Peanut Caramel filmed, ~50 cal per 1/4 bar)
To taste — sugar-free chocolate syrup (any brand)
1/4 of a peanut-caramel protein bar, chopped small (the second 1/4 for the topping)

recipeInstructions.name: Pour Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk to a Creami pint (or blending vessel).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sweetener
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Whey Isolate
recipeInstructions.text: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Guar Gum
recipeInstructions.text: 1/8 tsp guar gum, LEVEL measure. Heaped = gummy.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Salt
recipeInstructions.text: 1 pinch salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Powdered Peanut Butter
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tbsp powdered peanut butter (PB2, PBfit, or any brand). Series-first — no prior CCC episode used powdered peanut butter in the base. Powdered PB carries the peanut-butter-cookie flavor through the whole pint and stacks ~5g protein on top of the whey isolate.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Immersion blender until completely smooth. Zero lumps of powdered PB, uniform light-tan color from the peanut butter.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer to a Creami pint if you didn't build in the pint. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours. Do not exceed the max-fill line.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest 5 Min + First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes — NO hot-water bath. Process on Regular Ice Cream, NOT Lite. The first spin may look grainy; expected because the Respin (with protein-bar pieces) finishes the texture.

recipeInstructions.name: Chop Protein Bar
recipeInstructions.text: Chop 1/2 of a peanut-caramel protein bar into small pieces (~1/4 inch cubes) — half becomes the Respin mix-in, half becomes the post-scoop topping. Barebells Salty Peanut Caramel is filmed; any comparable peanut-caramel protein bar works (verify the current package for peanut / soy / dairy allergens).

recipeInstructions.name: Add Mix-in + Respin
recipeInstructions.text: Poke 1/4 of the chopped protein-bar pieces (half of what you chopped) into the surface of the first-spin pint (better distribution than piling on top). Run one Respin cycle WITHOUT adding liquid. Respin distributes the bar pieces AND finishes the grainy texture from the first spin. Series-first: this is the first CCC ep to use a protein BAR (not a protein brownie) as the Respin mix-in — the pre-formed caramel/chocolate/peanut chunks are what supply the SNICKERS identity in the pockets.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the finished pint into a bowl. Creamy peanut-butter-cookie base with visible protein-bar pieces pulled through.

recipeInstructions.name: Chocolate Drizzle
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle sugar-free chocolate syrup over the scoops to taste. Any brand works — chocolate syrup is intentionally brand-agnostic. Post-scoop only; don't try to Respin it in.

recipeInstructions.name: Bar Topping + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Scatter the remaining 1/4 of chopped protein bar over the top. Serve immediately — the bar topping stays crunchy against the creamy Creami, which is the SNICKERS payoff. Whole pint = 1 serving at ~370 cal / 53g protein.

recipe.name: Spicy Chicken Sandwich
recipe.description: 250 cal / 26g protein. One crispy air-fryer sandwich, almost no effort.
recipeIngredient: 1 frozen breaded chicken breast fillet — Episode 7 uses Bettergoods Original (140 cal / 16g protein); Kirkland is the preferred pick. Choose any fillet with at least 10g protein per 100 calories.
1 keto hamburger bun — Episode 7 uses Bettergoods (50 cal / 7g protein)
1 tbsp or less low-calorie spicy sauce — keep this at 20 cal or less for the stated macros

recipeInstructions.name: Cook The Fillet
recipeInstructions.text: Air fry the frozen chicken fillet per its package directions and verify it reaches 165°F. Crispy, not soggy — single layer, don't overcrowd.

recipeInstructions.name: Toast The Bun
recipeInstructions.text: Add the bun halves near the end and toast until lightly crisp.

recipeInstructions.name: Melt The Velveeta
recipeInstructions.text: Lay one Velveeta slice on the hot fillet and return it to the air fryer just until melted.

recipeInstructions.name: Sauce + Assemble
recipeInstructions.text: Spread up to 1 tablespoon low-calorie spicy sauce on the bottom bun, add the cheesy fillet, close the sandwich, and serve immediately.

recipe.name: Spicy Umami Fried Rice
recipe.description: Four-serving spicy fried-rice base made from cold Bone Broth Rice, eggs, chilies, and a fast umami sauce. About 340 cal / 16g protein per serving.
recipeIngredient: 4 servings cold Bone Broth Rice (~3 cups cooked, made ahead and refrigerated)
Thai chilies to taste (4 used in this batch), finely sliced
4 tsp avocado oil (or any neutral high-smoke-point oil)

recipeInstructions.name: Make The Sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Stir together soy + sambal + sesame chili oil + Umami Punch in a small bowl or ramekin. Set aside. This is the entire 'sauce step' — no cooking, no reduction.

recipeInstructions.name: Prep
recipeInstructions.text: Keep the cold rice ready, whisk the four eggs with the sliced Thai chilies, and chop the green onions and chives. The frying moves quickly.

recipeInstructions.name: Soft-scramble
recipeInstructions.text: Heat half the avocado oil in a wok over medium-high. Add the eggs and cook until softly set; leave them in the wok.

recipeInstructions.name: Toast The Rice
recipeInstructions.text: Add the remaining oil and cold Bone Broth Rice. Break up the clumps and cook over high heat so the rice toasts instead of steaming.

recipeInstructions.name: Sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Add the sesame chili oil, soy sauce, sambal, and umami seasoning. Toss continuously until the rice is evenly amber and no liquid remains.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Add the green onions and chives, toss just until combined, and adjust salt only if needed.

recipe.name: Split Plate Apple Pie Snack Box
recipe.description: Four apple-pie-inspired snack boxes with jerky, apples, yogurt dip, and cookies. About 240 calories and 18g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 4 jerky sticks or 8 mini jerkies — 1 stick or 2 minis per box
4 small apples or 2 regular apples, cut into kid-friendly pieces
2 containers high-protein yogurt — 1/2 container per box for dipping

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Line up 4 divided snack boxes.

recipeInstructions.name: Jerky
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 jerky stick or 2 minis to each box. Adjust the exact portion based on appetite.

recipeInstructions.name: Apple
recipeInstructions.text: Cut 1 small apple or 1/2 regular apple per box into age-appropriate pieces.

recipeInstructions.name: Yogurt Dip
recipeInstructions.text: Spoon 1/2 container of high-protein yogurt into each box as the apple dip.

recipeInstructions.name: Cookies
recipeInstructions.text: Add 2 chocolate chip cookies to each box, keeping them away from the yogurt compartment.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Seal all 4 boxes and refrigerate or pack with an ice pack until snack time.

recipe.name: Split Plate Berry Power-Up Snack Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 3 — no-cook kid snack with protein, fruit, cheese, and crunch. Beef stick + blueberries + Babybel + 28g pistachios. About 360 cal / 20g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 1 beef stick (Chomps or any — ~100 cal / 10g protein target)
1 handful blueberries (~30 cal / 0g protein for ~1/2 cup)
1 Babybel Original cheese (~70 cal / 4g protein per piece; check your pack)
28g shelled pistachios (~160 cal / 6g protein — see notes: for kids over 4 only)

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: 1 divided snack box (4-compartment Bento-style — same boxes as Snack Box Series Ep. 1 + Ep. 2).

recipeInstructions.name: Beef Stick
recipeInstructions.text: Slice 1 beef stick into kid-friendly bite-size pieces. Drop into the first compartment.

recipeInstructions.name: Blueberries
recipeInstructions.text: Rinse a handful of blueberries. Fill the second compartment.

recipeInstructions.name: Babybel
recipeInstructions.text: Unwrap 1 Babybel Original wedge. Drop into the third compartment (wax off, or leave wax on if the kid opens their own).

recipeInstructions.name: Pistachios
recipeInstructions.text: Measure 28g edible kernels after removing the shells (~1/4 cup). Add to the final compartment. Omit whole nuts for children under 4; see notes.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lid on. Refrigerate or pack with an ice pack until snack time. Serve chilled — Babybel and blueberries are best cold.

recipe.name: Split Plate Mediterranean Snack Box
recipe.description: Mediterranean-inspired kid snack box — prosciutto, Babybel, Castelvetrano olives, and almond-flour crackers. 4 boxes at once for 2 kids across 2 days. About 270 cal / 16g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 2 oz Del Duca prosciutto (or any prosciutto with comparable macros)
0.5 label serving Simple Mills Fine Ground Sea Salt almond-flour crackers
2 label servings Simple Mills almond-flour crackers

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Set out four divided snack boxes (4-compartment Bento-style — same format as Snack Box Series Ep. 1-4).

recipeInstructions.name: Prosciutto
recipeInstructions.text: Fold 2 oz prosciutto LOOSELY into one compartment of each box. Loose folds hold up better than tight rolls (less compression, more visual air).

recipeInstructions.name: Babybel
recipeInstructions.text: Drop one wrapped Original Babybel into the cheese compartment of each box. Keep the wax on — kids open their own, and the wax-peel ritual is part of the appeal.

recipeInstructions.name: Olives
recipeInstructions.text: Drain the Castelvetrano olives WELL (wet olives soak into other compartments). Divide 1.5 servings into the olive compartment of each box. FOR KIDS UNDER 4 — quarter lengthwise (see notes). Over 4 with good chewing = whole is fine but supervise.

recipeInstructions.name: Crackers
recipeInstructions.text: Add 0.5 serving Simple Mills almond-flour crackers to the DRY compartment of each box. Keep them dry — moisture from olives / prosciutto softens them.

KIDS HELP BUILD (optional but recommended): Let kids place the olives + crackers themselves. Turns exposure into low-pressure play. Doesn't guarantee they'll eat — just makes the food feel less unfamiliar.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lid on each box. Refrigerate — prosciutto + cheese need it. For lunchboxes, pack with an ice pack. Serve chilled.

recipe.name: Split Plate Pizza Snack Box
recipe.description: Four no-cook pizza snack boxes with turkey pepperoni, cubed cheese, crackers, and cucumber. About 220 calories and 15g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 3-4 servings turkey pepperoni (Hormel or Applegate — 3/4 to 1 serving per box)
4 cheese sticks (1 per box, cubed) — Sargento Colby-Jack shown
2 servings Triscuit Thin Crisps (1/2 serving per box)
1 large cucumber (sliced or chopped, to fill each box)
Optional at-home side: marinara for dipping (skip in the packed box to avoid mess)

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Line up 4 divided snack boxes (any brand with 3-4 compartments — the pastel Bento-style boxes shown work great).

recipeInstructions.name: Turkey Pepperoni
recipeInstructions.text: Add 3/4 to 1 serving of turkey pepperoni to one compartment of each box. Kid appetite determines the exact count — small kids get ~5-6 slices, bigger kids get the full serving.

recipeInstructions.name: Cheese Stick Cubes
recipeInstructions.text: Cube 1 cheese stick per box (Sargento Colby-Jack shown — mozzarella, sharp cheddar, or Monterey Jack also work). Add cubes to the next compartment.

recipeInstructions.name: Thin Crisps
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1/2 serving Triscuit Thin Crisps per box for the crackly pizza-crust texture. Any small savory cracker works if Triscuits aren't available.

recipeInstructions.name: Cucumber to Fill
recipeInstructions.text: Slice or chop cucumber and pack it into the remaining space in each box. Fresh crunch balances the salty savory side.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lids on, refrigerate until snack time. Serve cold. If serving at home, marinara on the side for dipping — keep it OUT of the packed box to avoid soggy crackers + messy cleanup.

recipe.name: Split Plate Ranch Crunch Snack Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 4 — higher-protein savory snack box. Turkey + cucumber + carrots + Harvest Snaps + Greek-yogurt-forward ranch dip. ~230 cal / 27g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 1 small container Fage 0% Greek yogurt (~5.3 oz single-serve, or 1 cup from a tub)
Simply Organic Ranch dip seasoning, to taste (~1 tbsp per batch)
1 portion ranch dip (~1/4 of the batch)
3 oz Hillshire Farm carved oven-roasted turkey (or any deli turkey)
1/2 serving Harvest Snaps Lightly Salted (~11g / ~11 pieces — half the label serving)
Baby carrots or carrot sticks, as needed

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: 1 divided snack box per person (4-compartment Bento-style — same box format as Snack Box Series Ep. 1-3). Build a batch of 4 in one pass.

recipeInstructions.name: Ranch Dip Base
recipeInstructions.text: Add the full container of Fage 0% Greek yogurt to a small mixing bowl. This is ~80% of the dip volume.

recipeInstructions.name: Sour Cream
recipeInstructions.text: Add 4 tbsp Daisy Light sour cream. DO NOT skip this — the light sour cream is what makes the yogurt taste like actual ranch instead of plain Greek yogurt with seasoning.

recipeInstructions.name: Season
recipeInstructions.text: Sprinkle Simply Organic ranch seasoning to taste (~1 tbsp per batch). Start light — taste after mixing.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix
recipeInstructions.text: Stir until thick, creamy, and evenly seasoned. Should look like actual ranch dip, not thin yogurt. Taste and add more seasoning if needed.

recipeInstructions.name: Portion Dip
recipeInstructions.text: Spoon ~1/4 of the batch into the dip compartment of each snack box.

recipeInstructions.name: Turkey
recipeInstructions.text: Fold 3 oz carved turkey into the largest compartment of each box. Loose fan-folds hold up better than tight rolls.

recipeInstructions.name: Cucumber
recipeInstructions.text: Slice cucumber into thin rounds (kid-friendly bite-size). Fill the produce compartment. FOR KIDS UNDER 4 — see notes for safe cut sizes.

recipeInstructions.name: Carrots
recipeInstructions.text: Add baby carrots or thick carrot sticks alongside the cucumber. Kids over 4 handle whole baby carrots; under 4, cut lengthwise (see notes).

recipeInstructions.name: Harvest Snaps
recipeInstructions.text: Fill the final compartment with 1/2 serving Harvest Snaps Lightly Salted per box (~11 pieces). If packing far ahead, add closer to serving so they stay crunchy.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lid on. Refrigerate or pack with an ice pack — the box has dairy (dip) + turkey and needs to stay cold.

recipe.name: Split Plate Tropical Chicken Snack Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 7 — the first hot-protein box in the series. Fully cooked fajita chicken + fresh mango + cubed Colby Jack + lightly salted cashews. About 250 cal / 21g protein per box. Make four at once for post-lunch or after-school hunger.
recipeIngredient: 2 oz fully cooked fajita chicken, chopped if needed
14g lightly salted cashews (~1/2 label serving, developmentally appropriate ages only)

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Set out four divided snack boxes (4-compartment Bento-style — same format as Snack Box Series Ep. 1-6). Fully cooked chicken means no stovetop or oven; the physical chicken package is source of truth if reheating before packing.

recipeInstructions.name: Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: Divide 2 oz fully cooked fajita chicken into one compartment of each box, chopped for the child's chewing ability. Any brand of fully-cooked seasoned chicken works (Soules Kitchen shown). If reheating, heat to 165°F and cool promptly before packing.

recipeInstructions.name: Mango
recipeInstructions.text: Peel and cut 1.5 mangoes total across the 4 boxes (3/8 mango each), age-appropriate pieces. The sweet-fresh anchor + the tropical hook. Any ripe mango variety (Ataulfo / Kent / Tommy Atkins) flexes.

recipeInstructions.name: Colby Jack
recipeInstructions.text: Cube one Colby Jack cheese stick per box and add to the third compartment. Cube size = 1/2-inch or smaller for young kids. Colby Jack is milder than sharp cheddar — kid-friendly by default.

recipeInstructions.name: Cashews
recipeInstructions.text: Add 14g lightly salted cashews (~1/2 label serving) to the final compartment. FOR KIDS UNDER 4 — omit whole cashews entirely; sub a soft alternative (soft berries, banana slices, or diced apple). Over 4 with good chewing = whole cashews only if supervised. The filmed brand contains cashews + peanut oil and may contain peanuts and other tree nuts.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lids on and refrigerate immediately — cooked chicken + fresh mango + cheese all need cold storage. Assembled boxes best within 2 days. For lunchboxes, pack with an ice pack. Add cashews closer to serving if maximum crunch matters (they soften in a sealed compartment after 24 hr).

recipe.name: Split Plate Vineyard Picnic Snack Box
recipe.description: No-cook 4-box snack prep — grapes, sliced beef stick, cubed cheddar, and pistachios. About 280 cal / 19g protein per box. The kids help fill the compartments.
recipeIngredient: 1 small handful grapes (prepared in an age-appropriate shape)
0.5 label serving pistachios (~85 cal per box, developmentally appropriate ages only)

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Set out four divided snack boxes (4-compartment Bento-style — same format as Snack Box Series Ep. 1-5). Invite the kids to help with the age-appropriate parts of the assembly.

recipeInstructions.name: Grapes
recipeInstructions.text: Divide 1 small handful of prepared grapes into one compartment of each box. FOR KIDS UNDER 4 — quarter lengthwise (see notes). Over 4 with confident chewing = whole grapes fine, supervise first few bites.

recipeInstructions.name: Beef Stick
recipeInstructions.text: Slice one beef stick per box into coins and divide into the next compartment. Coin slices > whole stick for kids (easier bites, less pressure to chew through a length).

recipeInstructions.name: Cheddar
recipeInstructions.text: Cube one cheddar cheese stick per box and add to the third compartment. Cube size = 1/2-inch or smaller for young kids. Creamy calcium + kid-familiar cheese flavor.

recipeInstructions.name: Pistachios
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1/2 label serving pistachios to the final compartment. FOR KIDS UNDER 4 — omit whole nuts entirely; sub a soft alternative (soft berries, banana slices, apple slices). Over 4 with good chewing = shell-off pistachios only, and supervise first few bites.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lid on each box. Refrigerate immediately — beef stick + cheddar both need cold storage. For lunchboxes, pack with an ice pack. Add pistachios closer to serving if maximum crunch matters.

recipe.name: Steak Quesadilla
recipe.description: Quick Lunches Ep. 6 — one crispy air-fryer steak quesadilla for National Quesadilla Day. ~270 cal / 24g protein for the whole thing.
recipeIngredient: 1 Mission Carb Balance flour tortilla, soft taco size (70 cal / ~6g protein)
1/2 serving Smoky Chipotle Crema (20 cal / ~1g protein; cross-link to /cookbook/smoky-chipotle-crema)
1 oz Velveeta Original shreds (60 cal / 5g protein)
2 oz Soule's Kitchen thinly sliced steak, fully cooked (80 cal / 12g protein)

recipeInstructions.name: Sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Spread 1/2 serving of Smoky Chipotle Crema across the tortilla.

recipeInstructions.name: Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Scatter the Velveeta shreds over one half of the tortilla.

recipeInstructions.name: Steak + Fold
recipeInstructions.text: Layer the ready-to-eat steak over the cheese and fold the tortilla into a half-moon.

recipeInstructions.name: Spray + Air-fry
recipeInstructions.text: Mist both sides with avocado oil and air fry until golden and crisp, flipping once.

recipeInstructions.name: Cut + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Slice into wedges and eat immediately while it's hot and melty.

recipe.name: Strawberry Brownie Cheesecake Snack Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 12 — dessert-inspired kid snack box: Oikos Triple Zero strawberry yogurt, Prime Bites red velvet protein brownie, Honey Maid graham crackers, fresh strawberries. ~230 cal / 19g protein per box.
recipeIngredient: 2 single-serve containers Oikos Triple Zero Strawberry Greek yogurt — divided across 4 boxes; 1/2 container per box
2 Prime Bites Red Velvet Protein Brownies — 1/2 brownie per box (~10g protein per half)
4 Honey Maid honey graham cracker sheets — 1 sheet per box (~60 cal per sheet)
Fresh strawberries — hulled and cut to fill each box

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Line up 4 divided snack boxes. Buluker pastel 4-compartment boxes shown — the same set featured on Favorites → Snack Box Essentials.

recipeInstructions.name: Strawberry Yogurt
recipeInstructions.text: Divide each Oikos Triple Zero container between 2 boxes — 1/2 container per box in one compartment. This is the creamy anchor + the fresh-strawberry dip.

recipeInstructions.name: Fresh Strawberries
recipeInstructions.text: Hull and cut fresh strawberries into kid-friendly bite pieces, then fill one compartment of each box. Strawberries + yogurt = the cheesecake half of the box.

recipeInstructions.name: Honey Graham
recipeInstructions.text: Place 1 Honey Maid honey graham cracker sheet in one compartment of each box. Break into smaller pieces for younger eaters if needed — the crackers stay crispest when packed WHOLE and broken at snack time.

recipeInstructions.name: Red Velvet Brownie
recipeInstructions.text: Cut each Prime Bites Red Velvet Protein Brownie in half and place one half in the remaining compartment of each box. The fudgy dessert element without a full dessert plate.

recipeInstructions.name: Seal + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lids on and refrigerate. Serve within 2 days. Transport with an ice pack for lunchbox use. Graham cracker softens in a closed box — pack a whole cracker and let the kid break it if you want crisper crunch.

recipe.name: Strawberry Shortcake Roll Protein Creami
recipe.description: CrumblCreamiCut Week 10 Flavor 3 — strawberry-emulsion protein Creami with Entenmann's pound-cake pieces and a Smucker's strawberry syrup finish. About 350 calories and 41g protein for the complete pint.
recipeIngredient: 1 batch usual protein Creami base (240 cal / 40g protein)
1/4 tsp strawberry emulsion (blend into base before freezing)
1/2 Entenmann's Pound Mini Snack Cake (full 39g cake is 160 cal / 2g protein)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Blend 1/4 teaspoon strawberry emulsion into your usual protein Creami base until completely smooth.

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint without exceeding the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level overnight.

recipeInstructions.name: First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Rest the pint 5 minutes, then process on Regular Ice Cream. If it stays powdery, run one no-liquid Respin before the mix-in.

recipeInstructions.name: Mix-in The Pound Cake
recipeInstructions.text: Cut a center well, press in half of one Entenmann's Pound Mini Snack Cake, and run Mix-In.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the Creami into a bowl.

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Finish with 1/2 tablespoon Smucker's Strawberry Flavored Syrup. Eat immediately for the intended texture.

recipe.name: Summer Moon-Inspired Protein Creamer
recipe.description: A homemade Moon Milk-inspired creamer with Nurri protein milk and four sugar-free syrup flavors — about 14 calories and 1.7g protein per 2 tablespoons.
recipeIngredient: 2 pumps (about 1 tbsp) Syruvia Sugar-Free White Chocolate Mocha syrup
2 pumps (about 1 tbsp) Syruvia Sugar-Free Irish Cream syrup
2 pumps (about 1 tbsp) Syruvia Sugar-Free Maple Bourbon Pecan syrup
2 pumps (about 1 tbsp) Syruvia Sugar-Free French Vanilla syrup

recipeInstructions.name: Combine
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the milk and two pumps of each syrup into a clean lidded jar.

recipeInstructions.name: Shake
recipeInstructions.text: Close the jar and shake until combined.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour
recipeInstructions.text: Add 2 tablespoons to brewed coffee. Stir or shake the batch again before each use.

recipeInstructions.name: Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Refrigerate promptly and follow the milk carton storage guidance. This is a cold-mixed dairy creamer, not shelf-stable.

recipe.name: Sunny-Side Eggs + Canadian Bacon Breakfast
recipe.description: A real hot breakfast in under 10 minutes — 3 sunny-side eggs + 5 Jones Canadian bacon slices, ~310 cal / 35g protein. The water-and-lid method sets the whites and keeps the yolks runny.
recipeIngredient: 5 slices Jones Canadian bacon, fully cooked (~100 cal / 16.7g protein; label lists 60 cal / 10g per 3 slices)
Light spray cooking spray (excluded from macros)
Small splash of water (for steaming the egg whites)

recipeInstructions.name: Spray + Heat
recipeInstructions.text: Lightly spray a skillet and set it over medium-low heat.

recipeInstructions.name: Crack + Season
recipeInstructions.text: Crack in three eggs. Separate the whites gently if they run together, then season.

recipeInstructions.name: Splash + Cover
recipeInstructions.text: Add a small splash of water and cover until the whites are set and the yolks remain runny. Transfer the eggs to a plate.

recipeInstructions.name: Warm The Bacon
recipeInstructions.text: Add five fully cooked Canadian bacon slices and warm about 1 minute per side.

recipeInstructions.name: Plate
recipeInstructions.text: Plate the Canadian bacon beside the eggs and serve immediately.

recipe.name: Sunshine Snack Box
recipe.description: Snack Box Series Ep. 9 — a warm-color palette snack box named for the yolk-yellow / strawberry-red / cheese-cream / peanut-tan color story. Boiled egg + dried strawberries + light cheese wedge + salted peanuts. About 280 cal / 16g protein per box. Make four for 2 kids × 2 days.
recipeIngredient: 1 large hard-boiled egg, peeled + sliced (halved or age-appropriate)
0.75 oz salted peanuts (developmentally appropriate ages only)

recipeInstructions.name: Set up
recipeInstructions.text: Set out four divided snack boxes (4-compartment Bento-style — same format as Snack Box Series Ep. 1-8). Have peeled hard-boiled eggs ready (make ahead — 4 large eggs boiled, ice-bathed, peeled — 10 min active + 12 min cook / cool). Ep. 9 continues the shelf-stable-protein pattern from Ep. 8: cook once, chill, hold.

recipeInstructions.name: Slice Eggs
recipeInstructions.text: Slice each peeled hard-boiled egg in half (over-4s) or into age-appropriate small pieces (under-4s). Yolk-yellow is the warm-color anchor for the whole box; keep the yolk exposed on top for the visual identity. 4 eggs across 4 boxes = 1 egg per box.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Eggs
recipeInstructions.text: Place 1 sliced egg into the first compartment of each box, yolk-side up when possible for the sunshine identity moment. Boiled egg is the ~6g protein anchor per box.

recipeInstructions.name: Strawberries
recipeInstructions.text: Add one 60-calorie portion of dried strawberries to the second compartment of each box. Dried strawberries are the sweet-hit + warm-red color anchor. Any brand of freeze-dried or dehydrated strawberries flexes — measure by label serving, not by handful, since portion size drives ~60 cal / portion.

recipeInstructions.name: Cheese Wedge
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 wrapped light cheese wedge to the third compartment of each box (Laughing Cow-style — creamy spreadable wedge, ~35-50 cal / 2-3g protein). Cheese-cream color completes the warm palette. Wrapped wedge stays clean in the box; kids can help unwrap at snack time.

recipeInstructions.name: Peanuts
recipeInstructions.text: Weigh 0.75 oz salted peanuts into the final compartment of each box (about a small handful — measure by weight, not by feel). Peanut-tan color completes the sunshine palette + adds crunch, fat, and a bit more protein. FOR KIDS UNDER 4 — omit whole peanuts entirely; sub a soft alternative (soft berries, banana slices, or diced apple). Over 4 with good chewing = whole peanuts only if supervised.

recipeInstructions.name: Lid + Chill
recipeInstructions.text: Snap lids on and refrigerate promptly. Serve within 2 days. Dried strawberries + peanuts may soften slightly in the sealed box's humidity — add peanuts closer to serving if maximum crunch matters (they hold OK for 2 days but the first-day crunch is best).

recipe.name: Tiramisu Iced Proffee
recipe.description: Proffee Episode 7 — a Nilla-and-chocolate rim, Ep 1's concentrate-first protein-coffee base, and a separate whipped Fage-vanilla cold foam that gives it the creamy tiramisu finish. ~180 cal / 24g protein per glass (range ~170-185), 5-minute build.
recipeIngredient: Very light sugar-free chocolate syrup, for coating the rim
2-3 Nilla wafers, crushed (wheat allergen — verify the current package)
1 tbsp instant coffee (creator's dose; use less for a milder drink)
1/2 scoop unflavored whey isolate (~14g protein — adjust by brand)
2-3 tbsp hot water (hot but NOT boiling)
1 tsp sugar-free vanilla Jell-O pudding mix

recipeInstructions.name: Rim The Glass
recipeInstructions.text: Coat the rim lightly with sugar-free chocolate syrup and crushed Nilla wafers. Reserve the leftover chocolate-Nilla mixture — it goes into the drink later, no waste.

recipeInstructions.name: Build The Concentrate
recipeInstructions.text: Froth instant coffee, monk fruit, 1/2 scoop unflavored whey isolate, 1/2 tsp vanilla, and 2-3 tbsp hot (not boiling) water until completely smooth. Blend the whey into the concentrate FIRST — the Proffee-series spine that prevents clumps.

recipeInstructions.name: Assemble
recipeInstructions.text: Add ice and 1/2 cup Fairlife fat-free milk to the concentrate.

recipeInstructions.name: Make The Foam
recipeInstructions.text: Separately froth 1 tbsp Fage 0%, 1 tsp sugar-free vanilla Jell-O pudding mix, and 1/8 cup Fairlife until thick and creamy.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Stir the reserved chocolate-Nilla rim mixture into the drink, spoon the vanilla cold foam over the top, and dust lightly with cocoa. Serve immediately.

recipe.name: TKS Sauce
recipe.description: Sweet heat + umami glaze. Macro-conscious takeout, six ingredients, two minutes.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Verka Organic Ginger Garlic Paste
1 tbsp Nakano Seasoned Rice Vinegar (Mild & Sweet)
2 tbsp Kikkoman All-Purpose Soy Sauce (1/8 cup)
1 packet Bare Bones Instant Chicken Bone Broth (15g, 10g protein)
1.5 tbsp Taste Flavor Co. Hot Honey Sriracha

recipeInstructions.name: Combine
recipeInstructions.text: Add ginger-garlic paste, sesame chili oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, bone broth packet (open it and pour the powder in), and hot honey sriracha to a small bowl or shaker bottle.

recipeInstructions.name: Whisk Aggressively
recipeInstructions.text: Until the bone broth powder fully dissolves — no clumps. The powder is what gives the sauce body; if it's not dissolved, the sauce stays thin and tastes flat.

recipeInstructions.name: Taste + Adjust
recipeInstructions.text: Too salty → add 1 tsp more vinegar OR 1 tsp more hot honey. Too sweet → add 1 tsp more soy. Too flat → bump the sesame chili oil to 3/4 tsp. Too thin → simmer 60 sec in a small pan (rare; usually the toss-in-hot-pan step at the dish level fixes this).

recipeInstructions.name: Ready to Use
recipeInstructions.text: For crispy chicken, pour around the edge of a hot dry skillet, add the cooked chicken, toss aggressively 60-90 sec until coated. The dry skillet + residual breading starch + sauce = natural cling, no slurry needed.

recipe.name: TKS Sweet Heat Chicken
recipe.description: Crazy Cuizine chicken + TKS Sauce. Drop the orange-sauce packet, gain a real glaze, keep the 20 minutes.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Crazy Cuizine Mandarin Orange Chicken (frozen, ~half the Costco party box)
*** Discard the included orange-sauce packet — that's a sugar bomb, you're swapping it out ***
1 batch TKS Sauce — make ahead while chicken cooks, takes 2 minutes

recipeInstructions.name: Air Fry The Chicken
recipeInstructions.text: From frozen, 400°F for 9-12 min. Shake basket halfway. Goal: crispy + golden, NOT soggy. Pull when the edges crack when squeezed (or follow box: 'fully cooked, ready in 20 min'). Single layer in the basket — overcrowding = steamed not crisp.

recipeInstructions.name: Make The Sauce
recipeInstructions.text: While chicken cooks (you have ~10 min). Whisk together ginger-garlic paste + sesame chili oil + rice vinegar + soy + bone broth packet + hot honey sriracha in a small bowl. Whisk hard — the packet powder needs to fully dissolve. (Full method on the TKS Sauce page.)
DUMP THE ORANGE PACKET. Seriously. The Crazy Cuizine box ships with a packet of sugary orange sauce. That's the part you're replacing. Throw it in the trash. This is the move.

recipeInstructions.name: Hot Dry Skillet — The Cling Step
recipeInstructions.text: Heat a large nonstick or carbon-steel skillet on medium-high. NO oil — pan dry. When the pan is screaming hot (water droplet beads + skitters), add the crispy chicken.

recipeInstructions.name: Toss With Sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Pour the TKS Sauce around the edge of the hot pan (not directly on the chicken). It will hiss + bubble immediately. Toss aggressively for 60-90 seconds. The residual breading starch + the sauce reduce and caramelize together — natural restaurant glaze, no cornstarch slurry needed. Off heat the moment every piece is glossy.

recipeInstructions.name: Plate + Garnish
recipeInstructions.text: Pile chicken on a plate or in a bowl. Scatter sliced scallions + toasted sesame seeds on top (optional but recommended — visual lift, fresh bite, takes 10 seconds).

recipeInstructions.name: Pair (optional But The Whole Point)
recipeInstructions.text: Serve over Spicy Umami Fried Rice for a complete dinner. Chicken alone = 480 cal / 36g protein per serving. With rice = ~810 cal / 52g protein. Real dinner, real macros.

recipe.name: 260-Calorie Toasted Roast Beef & Cheese Sandwich
recipe.description: Quick Lunches Ep. 2 — hot roast beef, melted Velveeta, toasted Sola bread, mustard. 260 cal / 34g protein in about six minutes.
recipeIngredient: 1 slice Velveeta Original (or any pasteurized prepared cheese slice)
2 slices Sola Sweet & Buttery bread (or any high-fiber sandwich bread)

recipeInstructions.name: Portion Beef
recipeInstructions.text: Lay 3 oz deli roast beef on a sheet of air-fryer-safe parchment. Loose folds, not stacked flat — helps the cheese melt into the layers instead of sliding off.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Cheese
recipeInstructions.text: Place 1 slice of Velveeta directly on top of the beef. The beef acts as the heat carrier; the cheese melts passively as the beef warms.

recipeInstructions.name: Air Fry
recipeInstructions.text: Run Air Fry mode for 5–6 minutes until the beef is hot throughout and the cheese fully melted. Do not invent a temperature — use your air fryer's Air Fry preset. Appliance settings vary.

recipeInstructions.name: Toast Bread
recipeInstructions.text: While the beef and cheese are in the air fryer, toast 2 slices of Sola Sweet & Buttery bread to your preferred crispness. Watch closely — low-carb bread browns fast at the edges.

recipeInstructions.name: Build
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer the hot roast beef and melted cheese onto one slice of toast in a single scoop with the parchment. Add yellow mustard to taste.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Close the sandwich, slice on the diagonal, serve immediately. The bread stays crisp; the cheese stays molten.

recipe.name: Two-Ingredient Sugar-Free Hot Fudge
recipe.description: Reusable dessert component — warm syrup + sifted Dutch cocoa, whisked silky in 30 seconds. Sub-15 cal, works on Creami pints, brownies, cakes, yogurt bowls.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp sugar-free maple syrup (Maple Grove Farms filmed)
1 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa powder (sift, don't dump)

recipeInstructions.name: Measure Syrup
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tbsp sugar-free maple syrup into a microwave-safe ramekin. Maple Grove Farms was filmed; any sugar-free syrup works.

recipeInstructions.name: Warm Syrup
recipeInstructions.text: Microwave 10-15 seconds. Don't overheat — overheated syrup sets too thick as it cools.

recipeInstructions.name: Sift Cocoa
recipeInstructions.text: Sift 1 tbsp Dutch cocoa into the warm syrup. Sifting is NOT optional — unsifted = gritty, sifted = silky.

recipeInstructions.name: Whisk
recipeInstructions.text: Whisk until no dry cocoa remains and the sauce reads silky and glossy. Aim for warm chocolate-syrup consistency.

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle immediately over the target dessert. Thickens as it cools — becomes a fudge shell over cold scoops.

recipe.name: Umami Lemon Heat Sauce
recipe.description: Creamy. Salty. Bright. Finishes with heat.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Smash Kitchen Organic Dijon Mustard
1 tsp Lee Kum Kee Chili Oil

recipeInstructions.name: Combine
recipeInstructions.text: Add everything to a bowl — mayo, lemon juice, soy, Dijon, chili oil.

recipeInstructions.name: Whisk
recipeInstructions.text: Whisk until smooth and fully combined. No streaks of mayo, no separated oil.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest
recipeInstructions.text: Let sit 5 minutes before using. Don't skip — this is when the flavors settle and stop tasting disjointed.

recipeInstructions.name: Taste + Adjust
recipeInstructions.text: More lemon = brighter. More soy = saltier. More chili oil = heat. Too thick? Add 1-2 tsp water. Too thin? Add 1 tsp more mayo.

recipe.name: Vanilla Chocolate Gelato Cookie Creami
recipe.description: Crumbl Creami Cut Week 7 — Vanilla Chocolate Gelato Cookie protein Creami with a brown-sugar base and the recipe-specific mix-ins.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp brown-sugar monk fruit / erythritol sweetener
1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1/2 waffle cone (break in AFTER Regular Ice Cream cycle)
1/2 waffle cone, broken over the scoops

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Base
recipeInstructions.text: Combine Fairlife 2% milk + brown-sugar monk fruit + whey isolate + guar gum + salt. Immersion blender until completely smooth. Brown-sugar sweetener is the Week 7 swap — matches the reference cookie's brown-sugar profile.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Pour into a Creami pint below the max-fill line. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest + Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes. Process on Regular Ice Cream cycle.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Waffle Cone After Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Break half a waffle cone into rough chunks. Make a narrow center well in the spun Creami, drop the chunks in.

recipeInstructions.name: Respin — no Liquid
recipeInstructions.text: Run Respin WITHOUT adding liquid. No-liquid Respin is what preserves the waffle-cone crunch; adding liquid softens the cone.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the Respun Creami into a bowl.

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle sugar-free chocolate syrup over the scoops. Move around the bowl so the drizzle laces the scoops rather than pooling in the center.

recipeInstructions.name: Second Cone Tier
recipeInstructions.text: Crumble the remaining half waffle cone directly over the scoops for a second crunch tier.

recipeInstructions.name: Shaved Chocolate + Eat
recipeInstructions.text: Finish with 40 calories worth of THIN shaved chocolate — shavings reach more bites than chips do at the same calorie budget. Eat immediately.

recipe.name: Chocolate Protein Rice-Paper Mochi
recipe.description: Viral Recipes Proteinized Ep. 6 — viral rice-paper mochi remade as a chocolate protein dessert. ~120 cal / 13g protein per piece when the filling is split four ways. Cocoa finish won; the filling doubles as a protein pudding.
recipeIngredient: 1 FAGE Total 0% plain Greek yogurt cup (150g)
45g PEScience Select Frosted Chocolate Cupcake protein powder
10g Jell-O Zero Sugar Chocolate Fudge pudding mix
Sugar-free chocolate syrup, for a light drizzle
Confectioners sugar, cocoa powder, or Oreo dust, for a light finish (cocoa preferred)

recipeInstructions.name: Mix The Filling
recipeInstructions.text: Mix the yogurt, protein powder, black cocoa, pudding mix, sweetener, and milk until completely smooth.

recipeInstructions.name: Chill (optional)
recipeInstructions.text: Chill the filling for 1 hour. This was done in the filmed batch and made the filling firmer and easier to wrap.

recipeInstructions.name: Soak The Rice Paper
recipeInstructions.text: Dip one rice-paper sheet in cold water for 10 to 15 seconds, just until pliable.

recipeInstructions.name: Fill + Fold
recipeInstructions.text: Place one quarter of the filling in the center and fold the rice paper into a compact parcel. Repeat to make four (only three were wrapped on camera).

recipeInstructions.name: Drizzle + Finish
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle lightly with sugar-free chocolate syrup and finish with confectioners sugar, cocoa, or Oreo dust. Cocoa was the preferred finish.

recipe.name: Viral Watermelon Ice Cream, Proteinized
recipe.description: Viral Recipes Proteinized Ep. 3 — 1/2 cup Nurri Whole + 1 tsp honey scraped inside a frozen mini-watermelon shell. Shared bowl: 105 cal / 10g protein. Fun once with kids, not a Creami replacement.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 mini watermelon, center hollowed to a small well and frozen overnight cut-side up
1/2 cup Nurri Whole Ultra-Filtered Protein Milk (85 cal / 10g protein — half the 1-cup 170/20 label)
1 tsp honey (~21 cal — needed for sweetness)

recipeInstructions.name: Freeze The Watermelon
recipeInstructions.text: Halve a mini watermelon. Scoop out just enough of the center to make a small well (a shallow bowl, not a giant hollow — the well only needs to hold ~1/2 cup of liquid). Place the half cut-side up on a sheet pan and freeze overnight.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour The Protein Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the frozen watermelon out of the freezer. Pour exactly 1/2 cup of Nurri Whole into the small frozen well. Don't assume every ready-to-drink protein shake will scrape the same way — Nurri Whole was chosen for its fat + protein blend.

recipeInstructions.name: Scrape Until Pink + Creamy
recipeInstructions.text: Use a spoon to scrape the frozen milk together with the small amount of frozen watermelon inside the well. Keep scraping until the mixture turns pink and granita-slushy — not ice-cream-smooth, more like snow-cone texture.

recipeInstructions.name: Honey + Share Immediately
recipeInstructions.text: Drizzle 1 tsp honey over the scraped dessert, scrape once more to marble it through, and serve straight from the watermelon shell with two spoons. Eat immediately — refreezing turns it icier and kills the trick.

recipe.name: Cookies and Cream Protein Ice Cream (Ninja Creami)
recipe.description: A vanilla protein ice cream with three sandwich cookies spun through and chopped cookies-and-cream protein chocolate on top. Freeze the base overnight, then spin and finish the pint. Inspired by a White Drop cookie for CrumblCreamiCut Week 4.
recipeIngredient: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate (~28g protein — adjust by brand)
1 tsp vanilla extract or vanilla emulsion
3 low-calorie sandwich cookies (HighKey Original filmed — verify current package for almond flour + allergens)
1/2 bar cookies-and-cream protein chocolate, chopped (Hormbles Chormbles Cookies & Cream filmed, ~50 cal per 1/2 bar)

recipeInstructions.name: Pour Milk
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 cup Fairlife 2% ultra-filtered milk to a blender or Creami pint.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sweetener
recipeInstructions.text: 2 tbsp monk fruit / erythritol sweetener.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Whey Isolate
recipeInstructions.text: 1 serving unflavored whey isolate.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Guar Gum
recipeInstructions.text: 1/8 tsp guar gum, LEVEL measure. Heaped = gummy.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Salt
recipeInstructions.text: 1 pinch salt.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Vanilla
recipeInstructions.text: 1 tsp vanilla extract or emulsion. Simplest CCC base variant to date — no cocoa, no emulsions, no berries, no powdered peanut butter, no Jell-O. The vanilla lets the cookie + protein chocolate do the identity work.

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Smooth
recipeInstructions.text: Blend until completely smooth. Zero lumps of whey, uniform pale-vanilla color.

recipeInstructions.name: Pour + Freeze (24 Hr)
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer to a Creami pint. Freeze upright and level for a full 24 hours. Do not exceed the max-fill line.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest 5 Min + First Spin
recipeInstructions.text: Pull the pint from the freezer, rest at ROOM TEMPERATURE for 5 minutes — NO hot-water bath. Process on Regular Ice Cream, NOT Lite. The first spin may look grainy; expected because the Respin (with sandwich cookies) finishes the texture.

recipeInstructions.name: Add Sandwich Cookies + Respin
recipeInstructions.text: Add 3 low-calorie sandwich cookies to the center of the pint (whole — the Respin breaks them into pieces). Run one Respin cycle WITHOUT adding liquid. Respin breaks the cookies into pieces AND distributes them AND finishes the grainy texture. Different mix-in category vs prior CCC eps (brownie / bar / candy).

recipeInstructions.name: Respin Result
recipeInstructions.text: The finished Respin should show visible cookie pieces distributed through the pale-vanilla pint with a smooth, non-grainy Creami texture. If the texture still reads powdery, run a second Respin.

recipeInstructions.name: Scoop
recipeInstructions.text: Scoop the finished pint into a bowl. Creamy vanilla Creami with visible sandwich-cookie pieces pulled through — cookies-and-cream from bite one.

recipeInstructions.name: Protein Chocolate Topping
recipeInstructions.text: Chop 1/2 bar of cookies-and-cream protein chocolate (Hormbles Chormbles filmed, ~50 cal). Scatter over the finished bowl. Do NOT process this topping through the machine — chopped on top only, so the chocolate pieces stay crunchy against the creamy base.

recipeInstructions.name: Taste Test + Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Whole pint = 1 serving at ~360 cal / 47g protein. Familiar cookies-and-cream identity — accessible, not a surprise flavor.

recipe.name: Zero-Calorie Shaved Ice Hack
recipe.description: Two ingredients, no machine: blend plain ice into snow, pack it into a cup, and finish with a zero-calorie-labeled water enhancer. A cold, sweet, occasional hot-day treat — not fruit, and not a nutritional stand-in for it.
recipeIngredient: Plain ice cubes (enough to fill your blender part-way; makes about one packed cup of snow)
Zero-calorie-labeled liquid water enhancer, to taste (MiO Fruit Punch used on camera)
Optional: a second zero-calorie-labeled water enhancer flavor for a two-color cup (cosmetic only)

recipeInstructions.name: Blend Ice to Snow
recipeInstructions.text: Blend plain ice cubes until they break down into a fine, fluffy snow. Scoop the snow into a cup and press it level.

recipeInstructions.name: Check The Label
